# GlassMarshmallow documentation

<!-- /docs/getting-started/introduction -->
# Introduction

GlassMarshmallow is a CSS framework with glass surfaces, light and dark mode and WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility (and AAA whenever possible) from the first component.

> **GlassMarshmallow is in development (v0.3).** The docs grow page by page together with the framework.

## What's included

- **Design tokens**: colors (the pastel palette with its scales), type, radii, shadows and glass as CSS custom properties with the `--gm-` prefix.
- **Base styles**: text, headings, an always-visible focus, the skip link and AAA accessibility rules built in.
- **Layout**: containers, breakpoints and a 12-column grid.
- **Components**: buttons, cards, alerts, tags, accordion, carousel, gallery, avatar, menu, search, tooltip, video player, progress bar, navbar and mobile tab bar.
- **Forms**: fields, segmented control, range, date picker, color picker and the rules for good forms.
- **Utilities** in the Tailwind style: spacing, sizing, borders, shadows, glass effects, animations, flex and display.
- **Optional scripts**, with no dependencies, for components that move (menu, calendar, carousel, player…).
- **Icons**: in their own package, [GlassMarshmallow Icons](/icons), with the same names as Bootstrap Icons.

The GlassMarshmallow logo is made with the framework too: [see how it was made](/docs/guides/logo).

## Quick start

Copy this page to start. It loads GlassMarshmallow and sets the color mode with `data-theme` on `<html>`.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="light">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <title>Hello, GlassMarshmallow</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow.min.css">
  </head>
  <body>
    <main class="gm-container">
      <h1>Hello, world!</h1>
      <button type="button" class="gm-btn">Get started</button>
    </main>
  </body>
</html>
```

## Accessibility

Every component meets **WCAG 2.2 AA** in light and dark mode, and almost everything reaches **AAA**: text reaches 7:1, everything you can press is 44 px, focus is always visible and everything works with the keyboard alone. More in [Accessibility](/docs/getting-started/accessibility).

## Next steps

- [Install GlassMarshmallow](/docs/getting-started/install) with a package manager or from a CDN.
- Read the framework's [approach](/docs/getting-started/approach) and the [user experience guides](/docs/guides/ux).
- Try the [tools](/tools): glass, gradient, filter and palette generators, and the TV effect.

<!-- /docs/getting-started/install -->
# Install

Use a package manager, a CDN or the source files to add GlassMarshmallow to your project.

## Package managers

Install the GlassMarshmallow CSS with your package manager of choice.

```sh:npm
npm install glassmarshmallow
```
```sh:pnpm
pnpm add glassmarshmallow
```
```sh:Yarn
yarn add glassmarshmallow
```
```sh:Bun
bun add glassmarshmallow
```

### Using the CSS

Link the compiled file in your HTML, or import it from your own CSS.

```html:HTML
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow.min.css">
```
```css:CSS
@import "glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow.css";
```

### Your CSS always wins

All the framework is inside a **CSS layer** called `glassmarshmallow` (`@layer`). Your own CSS, outside any layer, always wins over it, whatever its specificity and wherever you link it: a simple `.card { padding: 2rem; }` is enough to change a framework style, with no `!important` or long selectors.

```css:CSS
/* Wins over .gm-card, even though .gm-card is linked later */
.gm-card { border-radius: 0; }
```

If you also use layers, say the order once, at the top of your CSS. The later layer wins:

```css:CSS
@layer glassmarshmallow, my-styles;
```

### The font (optional)

GlassMarshmallow uses Montserrat. It comes in a separate file, `glassmarshmallow-font.min.css`, served from your own site (no Google Fonts). Add it before the framework if you want that font; if you prefer another one, leave it out and change `--gm-font` (see [Typography](/docs/customize/typography)).

```html:HTML
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow-font.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow.min.css">
```
```css:CSS
@import "glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow-font.css";
@import "glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow.css";
```

### Only the parts you need

`glassmarshmallow.css` has everything. If your site only uses some components, load the **core** (colors, base,
grid, theme, utilities and background) and then the **component families** you need. They can go in any order:
the framework's layers keep them in place.

```css:CSS
@import "glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow-core.css";
@import "glassmarshmallow/dist/css/components/basics.css";
@import "glassmarshmallow/dist/css/components/navigation.css";
```

| Family | Components | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `basics` | Button, card, alert, tag, code, avatar, accordion, progress, tooltip, dialog, round glass button, data list, hit area, copy command | — |
| `forms` | Form, field, range and slider, error summary, segmented control, calendar, color picker | `basics` |
| `navigation` | Navbar and tab bar, menu, search, full-screen menu, side menu, table of contents, previous/next, footers, social icons | `basics` |
| `media` | Video player, carousel, gallery, logo ticker | — |
| `chat` | Scroll row, chip, chat field, answer bubble, AI notice | — |
| `pages` | Section, hero, page structure, inner page, long text, code snippet, icon grid, showcase, documentation page | `basics` |
| `tools` | The generators' layout (`gm-tool`) | `basics`, `forms` |

Each file also has its `.min.css`. How much each one weighs is in [Performance](/docs/getting-started/performance).

## Icons

The icons live in their own package, [GlassMarshmallow Icons](/icons). With GlassMarshmallow 0.3 or later, use the icons 0.4 or later: they go in the framework's icons layer, so components and utilities can adjust them.

```sh:npm
npm install glassmarshmallow-icons
```
```sh:pnpm
pnpm add glassmarshmallow-icons
```
```sh:Yarn
yarn add glassmarshmallow-icons
```
```sh:Bun
bun add glassmarshmallow-icons
```

Then load the stylesheet and use an icon with two classes. Icons take the color of the text around them.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/glassmarshmallow-icons/font/glassmarshmallow-icons.css">

<i class="gmi gmi-moon" aria-hidden="true"></i>
```

## CDN

Skip the install and load the compiled CSS from a CDN.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/glassmarshmallow@0.3.0/dist/css/glassmarshmallow.min.css">
```

## Download

Download the source code from the [repository on GitHub](https://github.com/GlassMarshmallow/glassmarshmallow). The ready-to-use files are in `dist/css/` and the source files in `css/`.

To build `dist/` again after changing the source:

```sh
npm run css
```

## For AI tools & LLMs

GlassMarshmallow will come with files that help AI assistants write correct code with the framework:

- **`llms.txt`**: a short map of the docs for language models.
- **`AGENTS.md`**: the rules for agents working in the repository.
- **Skills**: ready-made instructions for common tasks.

Read more in [AI](/docs/getting-started/ai).

<!-- /docs/getting-started/ai -->
# AI

GlassMarshmallow is ready for AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot…) to use it well: they have the documentation in a format they understand and step-by-step guides for the most common tasks.

## Documentation for AI

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) | The index: what GlassMarshmallow is and the list of every page with one sentence each |
| [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) | All the documentation in a single text file |

They follow the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format. They are generated from this documentation every time the site is published, so they are always up to date.

To use them, give your assistant the address: “Read https://…/llms-full.txt and build me a contact form with GlassMarshmallow”.

## Skills

Step-by-step guides that teach an assistant to do specific tasks with GlassMarshmallow. They live in the repository's `skills/` folder:

| Skill | For |
| --- | --- |
| `install` | Add GlassMarshmallow to a project: CSS, icons, Montserrat, color mode and scripts |
| `customize-colors` | Change colors in light and dark mode without losing contrast |
| `create-component` | Add a new component to the framework with its design and accessibility rules |

With Claude Code, copy the skill folder into your project's `.claude/skills/` and it will be used when needed.

## AGENTS.md

The repository has an `AGENTS.md` file with the rules for agents working on the framework itself: where everything is, what must not be edited by hand, the accessibility to meet and how commits are named.

## What to ask for

- To use **only GlassMarshmallow classes and variables** (`gm-…`, `--gm-…`) and its icons (`gmi`), without inventing colors.
- To check **contrast in light and dark mode** and that everything works with the keyboard.
- To follow the [user experience guides](/docs/guides/ux) and the [form rules](/docs/forms/rules).

<!-- /docs/getting-started/approach -->
# Approach

The ideas behind GlassMarshmallow that guide every decision. If you are going to use it or add to it, start here.

## Glass and pastel

GlassMarshmallow's look comes from two things: **glass surfaces** (translucent background, blur and a thin border) and a **pastel palette** of 8 colors, plus black, white and grays. Everything else is restrained: Montserrat, light backgrounds by day and black at night, and a single accent color: pink by day and blue at night.

## Accessible from the start

- **WCAG 2.2 AA always**, in light and dark mode, and **AAA whenever possible**: 7:1 text, 44 px targets, visible and unobscured focus.
- It is checked with axe and by measuring contrast on the real pixels, not by eye.
- What cannot be made accessible does not go in.

## Light and dark, with the same care

Every color is a variable that changes with `data-theme`. Dark mode is not light mode inverted: it has its own tones so everything reads just as well.

## Mobile first

Unprefixed classes apply to every screen and prefixed ones (`gm-md-…`) are added from a [breakpoint](/docs/layout/breakpoints) upwards. On phones the navbar moves to the bottom tab bar.

## Components and utilities

- **Components**, like Bootstrap: ready-made pieces with one class (`.gm-btn`, `.gm-accordion`).
- **Utilities**, like Tailwind: small classes to adjust without writing CSS (`gm-mt-4`, `gm-shadow-md`).
- They combine: a component tweaked with utilities. How to use them, step by step, in [Building with utilities](/docs/getting-started/utilities).

## Plain CSS, optional JavaScript

- The framework is **plain CSS**: no Sass, no build step, no extra packages.
- It all goes in a **CSS layer** (`@layer glassmarshmallow`), so your own CSS always wins without fighting specificity ([Install](/docs/getting-started/install/)).
- Components that move (menu, calendar, carousel…) have an **optional script** with no dependencies. Without it, the component still shows and, whenever possible, works in a basic way.

## Names

- Everything starts with **`gm-`**: classes (`.gm-btn`) and variables (`--gm-accent`). That way it does not clash with other libraries.
- Components follow the **BEM** pattern: block, element and modifier (`.gm-player__button--main`).
- Sizes are **relative** (`rem`, `em`, `%`) so everything grows with the person's text size. Only the fine details are in `px` (1 px borders, shadows, blurs and the focus outline), so they stay thin when the text grows, as in Bootstrap and Tailwind.

## Own icons

Only [GlassMarshmallow Icons](/icons), with the same names as Bootstrap Icons. No emojis and no icons mixed in from other sets.

<!-- /docs/getting-started/utilities -->
# Building with utilities

GlassMarshmallow comes with **ready-made components**, like Bootstrap (`gm-btn`, `gm-card`, `gm-navbar`…), and **utilities**, like Tailwind: small classes that each do one thing. By combining utilities you can build any design of your own without writing CSS. This page explains how to use them; each topic then has its own page with all its classes (they are all in [Utilities](/docs/utilities/overview)).

## The idea

Instead of making up a class and writing its CSS…

```css:CSS
.my-notice { display: flex; gap: .75rem; padding: 1rem; border-radius: 1.25rem; }
```

…you put in the HTML the utilities that do the same:

```html
<div class="gm-d-flex gm-items-center gm-gap-3 gm-p-4 gm-rounded-md gm-bg-surface gm-shadow-md">
  <i class="gmi gmi-stars gm-text-xl" aria-hidden="true"></i>
  <p class="gm-m-0">Made only with utilities, without a line of CSS.</p>
</div>
```

That way the HTML shows what each thing looks like, there is no leftover CSS, and changes do not break other parts of the site.

## How to read the names

They all start with `gm-`, then **what they change** and, at the end, **how much**:

| Class | Reads as | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gm-mt-4` | margin (m) top (t), 4 | `margin-top: 1rem` |
| `gm-px-6` | padding (p) on the sides (x), 6 | `padding-inline: 1.5rem` |
| `gm-rounded-lg` | rounded corners, large | `border-radius: var(--gm-radius-lg)` |
| `gm-shadow-md` | medium shadow | a soft shadow |
| `gm-text-xl` | text, extra large | `font-size: 1.25rem` |
| `gm-d-flex` | display as flex | `display: flex` |

The numbers follow a **scale**: in spacing, **4 = 1 rem** (16 px), 2 = 0.5 rem, 8 = 2 rem. Using the scale keeps everything aligned and in proportion. The full table is in [Spacing](/docs/utilities/spacing).

## Depending on the screen size

Classes with no prefix always apply, starting with phones. With `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `xl` after `gm-`, they apply **from** that width up:

| Prefix | From |
| --- | --- |
| `gm-sm-…` | 600 px |
| `gm-md-…` | 860 px |
| `gm-lg-…` | 1100 px |
| `gm-xl-…` | 1300 px |

```html
<div class="gm-d-grid gm-grid-cols-1 gm-md-grid-cols-3 gm-gap-4">
  <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid gm-rounded-sm gm-p-4">One</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-mint gm-theme-solid gm-rounded-sm gm-p-4">Two</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-peach gm-theme-solid gm-rounded-sm gm-p-4">Three</div>
</div>
```

On a phone they go one under the other; from 860 px, in three columns. More in [Breakpoints](/docs/layout/breakpoints).

## Values that are not on the scale

If you need an exact value, write it **in brackets**: `gm-mt-[1.75rem]`, `gm-w-[18rem]`, `gm-bg-[#5cdfeb]`. And any CSS property without a utility, with `gm-[property:value]`. These classes are created by a small program that comes with the package:

```sh
npx glassmarshmallow build
```

How to set it up and what you can write, in [Arbitrary values](/docs/utilities/arbitrary).

## On hover, in dark mode…

With a **variant** in front, the class only applies in that case. They go with values in brackets:

| Variant | When it applies |
| --- | --- |
| `gm-hover:` | on mouse hover |
| `gm-focus-visible:` | when reached with the keyboard |
| `gm-dark:` / `gm-light:` | in dark / light mode |
| `gm-before:` / `gm-after:` | on the `::before` and `::after` layers |
| `gm-group-hover:` | when hovering the ancestor with `gm-group` |

```html
<a href="#" class="gm-d-inline-flex gm-items-center gm-gap-2 gm-px-6 gm-py-3 gm-rounded-full gm-bg-surface gm-shadow-md gm-transition gm-hover:translate-[0_-2px] gm-hover:shadow-[0_.75rem_2rem_rgb(0_0_0/.18)]">
  Lifts a little on hover <i class="gmi gmi-arrow-right" aria-hidden="true"></i>
</a>
```

The full list is in [Arbitrary values](/docs/utilities/arbitrary).

## Example: a card step by step

This is how a profile card is built with utilities only.

**1. The box:** background, padding, corners and shadow.

```html
<div class="gm-bg-surface gm-p-6 gm-rounded-lg gm-shadow-md gm-max-w-md">
  Sara Paez Yamuza
</div>
```

**2. The content in a row,** with a colored circle for the initials.

```html
<div class="gm-bg-surface gm-p-6 gm-rounded-lg gm-shadow-md gm-max-w-md gm-d-flex gm-items-center gm-gap-4">
  <span class="gm-d-grid gm-w-[3.5rem] gm-h-[3.5rem] gm-rounded-full gm-bg-linear-to-br gm-from-sky gm-to-lavender gm-place-items-center gm-font-bold" aria-hidden="true">SP</span>
  <div>
    <p class="gm-m-0 gm-font-bold gm-text-xl">Sara Paez Yamuza</p>
    <p class="gm-m-0 gm-muted gm-text-sm">Web designer and developer</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

**3. The details:** a framework button at the end and, on wide screens, more room in the card.

```html
<div class="gm-bg-surface gm-p-6 gm-md-p-8 gm-rounded-lg gm-shadow-md gm-max-w-md gm-d-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-4">
  <span class="gm-d-grid gm-w-[3.5rem] gm-h-[3.5rem] gm-rounded-full gm-bg-linear-to-br gm-from-sky gm-to-lavender gm-place-items-center gm-font-bold" aria-hidden="true">SP</span>
  <div class="gm-[flex:1]">
    <p class="gm-m-0 gm-font-bold gm-text-xl">Sara Paez Yamuza</p>
    <p class="gm-m-0 gm-muted gm-text-sm">Web designer and developer</p>
  </div>
  <a class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm" href="#">See portfolio</a>
</div>
```

The circle's gradient is made of utilities too: the direction (`gm-bg-linear-to-br`) and the colors (`gm-from-sky`, `gm-to-lavender`). How to make gradients, filters, masks or colored shadows is in the [Utilities](/docs/utilities/gradients) pages.

## Colors and dark mode

Utility colors come from the framework's variables, so they **change on their own** in dark mode (`data-theme="dark"`): there is nothing else to write.

```html
<div class="gm-d-grid gm-gap-2 gm-p-6 gm-rounded-lg gm-bg-surface gm-border gm-max-w-md">
  <p class="gm-m-0 gm-font-bold gm-text-body">Sara Paez Yamuza</p>
  <p class="gm-m-0 gm-text-muted">Easy to read in light and dark mode.</p>
  <p class="gm-m-0"><span class="gm-tag gm-bg-sky">Design</span> <span class="gm-text-sky gm-font-semibold">Sky text</span></p>
</div>
```

- `gm-bg-surface`, `gm-bg-body`, `gm-text-body`, `gm-text-muted`, `gm-border`… are the colors of the page, the cards, the text and the lines in each mode.
- Palette colors come ready to read: `gm-bg-sky` sets the pastel **and** the black text on top, and `gm-text-sky` uses the dark shade of sky, which meets the contrast.
- For something **different** in one mode only, use the `gm-dark:` or `gm-light:` variant with an arbitrary value: `gm-dark:bg-[#0b0b0c]`.
- A color written by hand (`gm-bg-[#ffffff]`) does **not** change with the mode. Better use the framework's ones, or add its dark version with `gm-dark:`.

All the colors are in [Text color](/docs/color/text), [Background](/docs/color/background) and [Light and dark mode](/docs/color/color-modes).

## Changing the scale for the whole site

Utilities and components use the same variables (`--gm-radius-lg`, `--gm-shadow-md`, `--gm-sky`, `--gm-font`…). If you change a variable, **every** class and component that uses it changes, without touching the HTML:

```html-code
<style>
  /* The whole site: less rounded medium corners and another font */
  :root { --gm-radius-md: 1rem; --gm-font: "Inter", sans-serif; }
  /* Dark mode only: a less black background */
  [data-theme="dark"] { --gm-bg: #0b0b0c; }
  /* Only inside one part: another accent color */
  .my-shop { --gm-accent: #8c57e9; }
</style>
```

With that, `gm-rounded-md`, the cards (`gm-card`) and the other pieces with medium corners change at once. The spacing numbers (`gm-p-4`, `gm-mt-8`…) are fixed so everything stays aligned; if you need another size, use an arbitrary value (`gm-p-[1.125rem]`). The list of variables is in [CSS variables](/docs/getting-started/css-variables).

## Accessibility when you build it yourself

Components already meet WCAG 2.2; when you build something with utilities, that is up to you. What is most often forgotten:

- **Keyboard focus.** The framework draws an outline when you arrive with the keyboard (`:focus-visible`). Do not remove it with `gm-[outline:none]`; if you want another one, change it with `gm-focus-visible:`.
- **Contrast.** Text needs 4.5:1 on its background (3:1 if it is large, and for borders and icons). The framework's colors already meet it; if you write one by hand, check it.
- **Tap size.** What can be pressed must be at least 44 × 44 px. If a button or an icon is smaller, add [`gm-hit-area`](/docs/helpers/hit-area), which makes the area bigger without changing how it looks.
- **Links inside text,** underlined: they should not stand out by color only.
- **Decorative icons,** with `aria-hidden="true"`; if an icon is alone in a button, the button gets an `aria-label`.
- **Motion.** The framework's animations turn off on their own if the person asked for it; if you make your own, add them with `gm-motion-safe:`.

All the rules are in [Accessibility](/docs/getting-started/accessibility).

## Component or utilities?

- **Use a component** when what you need already exists (a button, a menu, a calendar): it is tested, accessible and has its dark mode.
- **Use utilities** to place components (margins, columns, alignment) and to build what does not exist.
- **Mix them:** a component is adjusted with utilities, as in `<a class="gm-btn gm-mt-4 gm-w-full">`. Utilities come after components in the CSS, so they usually win and are good for changing a detail.
- If you repeat the same group of classes many times, move it to a component of your site (in Angular, React, Astro…) or to a class in your CSS.

## Your CSS always wins

The whole framework is in the `@layer glassmarshmallow` layer. If you prefer to write CSS for something, your CSS always wins, with no `!important` or long selectors. You can use only utilities, only your CSS, or both. More in [Install](/docs/getting-started/install).

<!-- /docs/getting-started/css-variables -->
# CSS variables

All of GlassMarshmallow's look comes from CSS variables with the `--gm-` prefix. They change on their own with light and dark mode (`data-theme`), and you can change them for the whole site or for just one part.

## Changing a variable

In `:root` for the whole site, in `[data-theme="dark"]` for dark mode, or on any element to change it only inside it:

```html-code
<style>
  :root { --gm-radius-md: 16px; }
  [data-theme="dark"] { --gm-bg: #0b0b0c; }
  .my-section { --gm-accent: #8c57e9; }
</style>
```

If you change a color, check the contrast afterwards (7:1 for text, 3:1 for borders and icons).

These are the main ones. The pastel palette and its scales are in [Palette](/docs/color/colors).

## Page and text

| Variable | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--gm-bg` | `#f5f5f7` | `#000` |
| `--gm-text` | `#1d1d1f` | `#f5f5f7` |
| `--gm-text-secondary` | `#3a3a3c` | `#d1d1d6` |
| `--gm-muted` | `#48484a` | `#b8b8bc` |
| `--gm-link` | `#004b96` | `#79beff` |
| `--gm-link-hover` | `#004b96` | `#79beff` |
| `--gm-selection` | `rgba(255, 166, 209, .45)` | `rgba(138, 180, 255, .35)` |
| `--gm-font` | `"Montserrat", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFo…` | same |
| `--gm-font-mono` | `ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace` | same |

## Surfaces and lines

| Variable | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--gm-surface` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, .82)` | `rgba(28, 28, 30, .82)` |
| `--gm-surface-solid` | `#fff` | `#1c1c1e` |
| `--gm-surface-glass` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, .86)` | `rgba(44, 44, 46, .86)` |
| `--gm-surface-glass-border` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, .8)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, .06)` |
| `--gm-surface-soft` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, .6)` | `rgba(44, 44, 46, .6)` |
| `--gm-line` | `rgba(0, 0, 0, .08)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, .1)` |
| `--gm-line-strong` | `#bbb` | `#545458` |
| `--gm-hover` | `rgba(0, 0, 0, .05)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, .08)` |
| `--gm-tag` | `#e8e8ed` | `#2c2c2e` |
| `--gm-tag-hover` | `#dcdce1` | `#3a3a3c` |
| `--gm-fill-subtle` | `rgba(0, 0, 0, .025)` | `rgba(255, 255, 255, .04)` |

## Accent and buttons

| Variable | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--gm-accent` | `#c71c6f` | `#8ab4ff` |
| `--gm-accent-strong` | `#940061` | `#003290` |
| `--gm-accent-hover` | `#700148` | `#00236b` |
| `--gm-focus` | `#c71c6f` | `#8ab4ff` |
| `--gm-primary` | `#1d1d1f` | `#f5f5f7` |
| `--gm-on-primary` | `#fff` | `#1d1d1f` |

### Another accent color

The accent is the color of accent buttons, keyboard focus, fields while typing, sliders and checkboxes. To change it for the whole site, give a value for each mode. For example, in lavender:

```html-code
<style>
  :root {
    --gm-accent: #6d47e5;          /* lavender 700: 5.6:1 on white */
    --gm-accent-strong: #490795;   /* background of accent buttons, with white text (AAA) */
    --gm-accent-hover: #350170;
    --gm-focus: #6d47e5;
    --gm-field-focus: #6d47e5;
    --gm-field-ring: rgba(109, 71, 229, .15);
  }
  [data-theme="dark"] {
    --gm-accent: #b9a3ff;          /* lavender: 8.9:1 on black */
    --gm-accent-strong: #490795;
    --gm-accent-hover: #350170;
    --gm-focus: #b9a3ff;
    --gm-field-focus: #b9a3ff;
    --gm-field-ring: rgba(185, 163, 255, .45);
  }
</style>
```

This is how it looks (with the day values):

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-5 gm-p-5 gm-rounded-sm gm-bg-body" data-theme="light" style="--gm-accent: #6d47e5; --gm-accent-strong: #490795; --gm-accent-hover: #350170; --gm-focus: #6d47e5; --gm-field-focus: #6d47e5">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--accent">Send</button>
  <input class="gm-range" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="60" aria-label="Volume" style="--gm-range-progress: 60%; width: 10rem">
  <div class="gm-check"><label><input type="checkbox" checked> I agree</label></div>
</div>
```

Check the contrast: the accent on the background, 3:1 at least (4.5:1 if you use it for text); white text on `--gm-accent-strong`, 7:1.

## States

| Variable | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |

| `--gm-warning` | `var(--gm-lemon-800)` | `var(--gm-lemon)` |

<!-- /docs/getting-started/accessibility -->
# Accessibility

GlassMarshmallow follows **WCAG 2.2 at level AA** in light and dark mode, the level asked for by European and Spanish law, and also meets the AAA criteria for contrast, presentation, focus and target size. These are all the rules, grouped by the four principles of WCAG, with how the framework meets each one.

> The complete list, with the 86 criteria of levels A, AA and AAA, is in [All the rules (WCAG 2.2)](/docs/getting-started/wcag).

> **The framework helps, but it does not do everything.** Your content (texts, images, names of buttons, order of the headings) also has to follow these rules.

## Perceivable

Everyone can see or hear the content.

| Criterion | Level | Rule | In GlassMarshmallow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.1.1 | A | Every image that gives information has a text alternative (`alt`). Decorative images and icons have `alt=""` or `aria-hidden="true"`. | Icons (`.gmi`) are decorative: they always go with `aria-hidden="true"`. |
| 1.3.1 | A | The structure is in the HTML: headings, lists, tables, labels and regions (`header`, `main`…). | See [Page structure](/docs/content/structure). Every field has its `<label>`. |
| 1.3.5 | AA | Fields about the person say what they ask for with `autocomplete` (name, email, tel…). | The examples of [Field](/docs/forms/field) use it. |
| 1.4.1 | A | Color is never the only way to give information: add a word, an icon or an underline. | Alerts carry an icon and a text; links inside text are underlined. |
| 1.4.3 | AA | Text has a contrast of at least 4.5:1 with its background, and large text (24 px, or 19 px in bold) at least 3:1. | Every color of the framework is measured in light and dark mode. See [Palette](/docs/color/colors). |
| 1.4.6 | AAA | Text has a contrast of at least 7:1, and large text 4.5:1. | All the text colors of the framework reach 7:1. Exceptions: solid backgrounds `gray-500` and `gray-600` (5.2:1 and 6:1) and the title of the home page in light mode, with the colors of the logo. |
| 1.4.4 | AA | The page works with the text at 200 % zoom. | Sizes in `rem` and `em`, so they grow with the text. |
| 1.4.8 | AAA | Blocks of text: lines of 80 characters at most, not justified, line height of 1.5, and colors chosen by the person. | Paragraphs and lists up to 80 characters, aligned to the start; with the high contrast mode of the system, its colors are used. |
| 1.4.10 | AA | At 320 px wide (or 400 % zoom) everything can be read without scrolling sideways. | Every page is checked at 320 and 375 px. |
| 1.4.11 | AA | Borders of fields and controls, focus and the parts of a chart have a contrast of at least 3:1. | Fields: 3.5:1 in light and 3.9:1 in dark. Focus: 4.9:1 and 7.5:1. |
| 1.4.12 | AA | The content still works if the user increases the spacing between lines, letters and words. | No fixed heights on boxes with text. |
| 1.4.13 | AA | Content that appears on hover or focus (tooltips) can be closed with Escape, stays while the pointer is on it and does not vanish by itself. | See [Tooltip](/docs/components/tooltip). |

## Operable

Everyone can use the page, with or without a mouse.

| Criterion | Level | Rule | In GlassMarshmallow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2.1.1 | A | Everything can be used with the keyboard alone. | Native buttons, links and fields; the calendar works with arrows, Home/End and Page Up/Down. |
| 2.1.2 | A | The keyboard never gets trapped: you can always leave a component with Tab or Escape. | Dialogs open with `showModal()` and close with Escape. |
| 2.2.2 | A | Anything that moves for more than 5 seconds can be paused. | The framework has no automatic animations. |
| 2.3.3 | AAA* | With «reduce motion» in the system, animations are removed. | Transitions are turned off with `prefers-reduced-motion`. (*AAA, but we always do it.) |
| 2.4.1 | A | There is a way to skip the menu and go straight to the content. | `.gm-skip-link`, the first link of the page. |
| 2.4.2 | A | Every page has a title that says what it is. | «Page name | GlassMarshmallow». |
| 2.4.3 | A | The focus moves in a logical order, the same as the reading order. | The HTML order is the visual order: no `tabindex` greater than 0. |
| 2.4.4 | A | Each link says where it goes (no «click here»). | — |
| 2.4.6 | AA | Headings and labels describe their content. | — |
| 2.4.7 | AA | The keyboard focus is always visible. | A 2 px outline, pink by day and blue at night, on everything that can be focused. |
| 2.4.11 | AA | The element with the focus is not hidden behind other content (fixed headers, bars). | The page keeps a scroll margin the height of the top bar (and of the bottom bar on mobile). |
| 2.4.12 | AAA | No part of the focused element is hidden. | The same scroll margin keeps it whole in view. |
| 2.5.3 | A | The accessible name of a button contains its visible text. | «‹ Back» is read as «Back: Tools». |
| 2.5.8 | AA | Everything you press measures at least 24 × 24 px. | Everything reaches 44 px (see 2.5.5). |
| 2.5.5 | AAA | Everything you press measures at least 44 × 44 px. | Buttons, menus, calendar days and options measure 44 px; small buttons and pills have an invisible layer that makes the area bigger. |

## Understandable

The content and how it works are easy to understand.

| Criterion | Level | Rule | In GlassMarshmallow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.1.1 | A | The page says its language with `lang` in `<html>`. | — |
| 3.1.2 | AA | A part in another language says it with `lang`. | — |
| 3.2.3 | AA | The navigation is in the same place and order on every page. | `.gm-navbar` and `.gm-tabbar` are the same everywhere. |
| 3.3.1 | A | Errors in a form are shown in text, next to the field, and say which field. | `.gm-field__error` with `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`. |
| 3.3.2 | A | Every field has a visible label, and required fields are marked. | — |
| 3.3.3 | AA | The error message says how to fix it. | «Write a complete email, for example sara@example.com». |
| 3.3.8 | AA | Logging in does not depend on remembering or copying anything (password managers and pasting work). | Password fields with `autocomplete="current-password"`. |

## Robust

It works with browsers and assistive technology.

| Criterion | Level | Rule | In GlassMarshmallow |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1.2 | A | Every control has a name, a role and a state that screen readers can read. | Native elements first; `aria-pressed`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-current` where they are needed. |
| 4.1.3 | AA | Messages that appear without moving the focus («Copied», «3 results») are announced. | A visually hidden text with `aria-live="polite"`. |

## How we check it

- **axe-core** on every page, in light and dark mode: 0 errors.
- **Contrast on the real pixels** when there is something behind the text (glass, lights, images), because automatic tools can’t see it.
- **Keyboard only**: every page is used with Tab, Shift + Tab, Enter, Space, Escape and the arrows.
- **Widths of 320, 375 and 1300 px**, without scrolling sideways.
- **Reduce motion** turned on in the system.

## Tools to check your page

- [axe DevTools](https://www.deque.com/axe/devtools/) and [WAVE](https://wave.webaim.org/extension/): browser extensions that review the whole page.
- Lighthouse, in the developer tools of Chrome.
- [Colour Contrast Analyser](https://www.tpgi.com/color-contrast-checker/): an eyedropper to measure the contrast of any point of the screen.
- VoiceOver (macOS and iOS) or NVDA (Windows), to hear the page as a screen reader user does.

<!-- /docs/getting-started/wcag -->
# All the rules (WCAG 2.2)

The 86 success criteria of WCAG 2.2, at levels A, AA and AAA, explained in plain words. Check this list every time you add something new to the framework, so that it meets them from the start.

> **Levels.** A is the minimum, AA is what the law asks for (and what GlassMarshmallow promises), and AAA is the most demanding. Criterion 4.1.1 (Parsing) was removed in WCAG 2.2.


## 1. Perceivable

| Criterion | Level | What it asks | State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1.1.1** Non-text content | A | Images and controls without text have a text alternative. | Your content |
| **1.2.1** Audio-only and video-only (prerecorded) | A | A recorded audio has a transcript; a video without sound has a description or transcript. | Not applicable |
| **1.2.2** Captions (prerecorded) | A | Recorded videos with sound have captions. | Not applicable |
| **1.2.3** Audio description or media alternative (prerecorded) | A | What is only seen in a video is explained in audio or in text. | Not applicable |
| **1.2.4** Captions (live) | AA | Live videos have captions. | Not applicable |
| **1.2.5** Audio description (prerecorded) | AA | Recorded videos have an audio description of what is only seen. | Not applicable |
| **1.2.6** Sign language (prerecorded) | AAA | Recorded videos have sign language interpretation. | Not applicable |
| **1.2.7** Extended audio description (prerecorded) | AAA | The video pauses when there is no gap for the audio description. | Not applicable |
| **1.2.8** Media alternative (prerecorded) | AAA | Recorded videos have a full text version. | Not applicable |
| **1.2.9** Audio-only (live) | AAA | Live audio has a text alternative. | Not applicable |
| **1.3.1** Info and relationships | A | The structure (headings, lists, tables, labels, regions) is in the HTML, not only in the look. | Meets |
| **1.3.2** Meaningful sequence | A | The reading order of the HTML makes sense. | Meets |
| **1.3.3** Sensory characteristics | A | Instructions don’t depend only on shape, size, position or sound («the round button on the right»). | Your content |
| **1.3.4** Orientation | AA | The page works in portrait and landscape. | Meets |
| **1.3.5** Identify input purpose | AA | Fields about the person use `autocomplete`. | Your content |
| **1.3.6** Identify purpose | AAA | The purpose of regions, icons and controls can be read by programs. | Meets |
| **1.4.1** Use of color | A | Color is never the only way to give information. | Meets |
| **1.4.2** Audio control | A | Audio that plays by itself for more than 3 seconds can be stopped. | Not applicable |
| **1.4.3** Contrast (minimum) | AA | Text 4.5:1; large text 3:1. | Meets |
| **1.4.4** Resize text | AA | The page works with the text at 200 %. | Meets |
| **1.4.5** Images of text | AA | Text is real text, not an image (except logos). | Your content |
| **1.4.6** Contrast (enhanced) | AAA | Text 7:1; large text 4.5:1. | Meets |
| **1.4.7** Low or no background audio | AAA | Speech in audio has little or no background sound. | Not applicable |
| **1.4.8** Visual presentation | AAA | Text blocks: lines of 80 characters at most, not justified, line height 1.5, user-chosen colors. | Meets |
| **1.4.9** Images of text (no exception) | AAA | No images of text except logos. | Your content |
| **1.4.10** Reflow | AA | At 320 px everything can be read without scrolling sideways. | Meets |
| **1.4.11** Non-text contrast | AA | Borders of controls, focus and parts of charts: 3:1. | Meets |
| **1.4.12** Text spacing | AA | It still works with more space between lines, letters, words and paragraphs. | Meets |
| **1.4.13** Content on hover or focus | AA | Tooltips can be closed with Escape, can be hovered and don’t vanish by themselves. | Meets |

## 2. Operable

| Criterion | Level | What it asks | State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **2.1.1** Keyboard | A | Everything works with the keyboard. | Meets |
| **2.1.2** No keyboard trap | A | You can always leave a component with the keyboard. | Meets |
| **2.1.3** Keyboard (no exception) | AAA | Absolutely everything works with the keyboard, with no exception. | Meets |
| **2.1.4** Character key shortcuts | A | Shortcuts of a single letter can be turned off or changed. | Meets |
| **2.2.1** Timing adjustable | A | Time limits can be turned off, adjusted or extended. | Your content |
| **2.2.2** Pause, stop, hide | A | What moves, blinks or updates by itself can be paused. | Meets |
| **2.2.3** No timing | AAA | There are no time limits. | Your content |
| **2.2.4** Interruptions | AAA | Interruptions (alerts, updates) can be postponed. | Your content |
| **2.2.5** Re-authenticating | AAA | If the session expires, no data is lost when you log in again. | Your content |
| **2.2.6** Timeouts | AAA | You are warned of how long you can be inactive before losing data. | Your content |
| **2.3.1** Three flashes or below threshold | A | Nothing flashes more than three times per second. | Meets |
| **2.3.2** Three flashes | AAA | Nothing flashes more than three times per second, of any size. | Meets |
| **2.3.3** Animation from interactions | AAA | Animations caused by the user can be turned off («reduce motion»). | Meets |
| **2.4.1** Bypass blocks | A | A way to skip repeated blocks (skip link, regions). | Meets |
| **2.4.2** Page titled | A | Each page has a title that says what it is. | Meets |
| **2.4.3** Focus order | A | The focus moves in a logical order. | Meets |
| **2.4.4** Link purpose (in context) | A | Each link says where it goes, with its text or the sentence around it. | Your content |
| **2.4.5** Multiple ways | AA | There is more than one way to find a page (menu, search, links). | Meets |
| **2.4.6** Headings and labels | AA | Headings and labels describe their content. | Your content |
| **2.4.7** Focus visible | AA | The keyboard focus is always visible. | Meets |
| **2.4.8** Location | AAA | You can tell where you are in the site (current page in the menu, breadcrumbs). | Meets |
| **2.4.9** Link purpose (link only) | AAA | The text of the link alone says where it goes. | Your content |
| **2.4.10** Section headings | AAA | Each section of content has a heading. | Your content |
| **2.4.11** Focus not obscured (minimum) | AA | The focused element is not completely hidden by fixed bars. | Meets |
| **2.4.12** Focus not obscured (enhanced) | AAA | No part of the focused element is hidden. | Meets |
| **2.4.13** Focus appearance | AAA | The focus outline is at least 2 px thick and has 3:1 contrast with and without focus. | Meets |
| **2.5.1** Pointer gestures | A | What needs gestures with several fingers or a path also works with a single tap. | Meets |
| **2.5.2** Pointer cancellation | A | Actions happen when you release, so you can cancel by moving away. | Meets |
| **2.5.3** Label in name | A | The accessible name contains the visible text. | Meets |
| **2.5.4** Motion actuation | A | What works by shaking or tilting the device also works with a button. | Not applicable |
| **2.5.5** Target size (enhanced) | AAA | Everything you press measures at least 44 × 44 px. | Meets |
| **2.5.6** Concurrent input mechanisms | AAA | You can use mouse, keyboard and touch at the same time. | Meets |
| **2.5.7** Dragging movements | AA | What is done by dragging can also be done without dragging. | Meets |
| **2.5.8** Target size (minimum) | AA | Everything you press measures at least 24 × 24 px. | Meets |

## 3. Understandable

| Criterion | Level | What it asks | State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **3.1.1** Language of page | A | The page says its language with `lang`. | Your content |
| **3.1.2** Language of parts | AA | Parts in another language say it with `lang`. | Your content |
| **3.1.3** Unusual words | AAA | Unusual words and jargon are explained. | Your content |
| **3.1.4** Abbreviations | AAA | Abbreviations are explained (for example with `<abbr>`). | Your content |
| **3.1.5** Reading level | AAA | Difficult texts have a simpler version. | Your content |
| **3.1.6** Pronunciation | AAA | When the pronunciation changes the meaning, it is explained. | Your content |
| **3.2.1** On focus | A | Receiving the focus does not change the page or the context. | Meets |
| **3.2.2** On input | A | Changing a field does not change the context without warning. | Meets |
| **3.2.3** Consistent navigation | AA | Menus are in the same place and order on every page. | Meets |
| **3.2.4** Consistent identification | AA | The same function has the same name and icon everywhere. | Meets |
| **3.2.5** Change on request | AAA | Big changes (new window, new page) only happen when the user asks. | Meets |
| **3.2.6** Consistent help | A | Help (contact, chat, FAQ) is in the same place on every page. | Your content |
| **3.3.1** Error identification | A | Errors are shown in text and say which field. | Meets |
| **3.3.2** Labels or instructions | A | Fields have labels, and instructions when needed. | Meets |
| **3.3.3** Error suggestion | AA | The error message says how to fix it. | Your content |
| **3.3.4** Error prevention (legal, financial, data) | AA | Important sends can be reviewed, corrected or undone. | Your content |
| **3.3.5** Help | AAA | There is help for filling in forms. | Your content |
| **3.3.6** Error prevention (all) | AAA | Every send can be reviewed, corrected or undone. | Your content |
| **3.3.7** Redundant entry | A | You don’t have to type again what you already gave in the same process. | Your content |
| **3.3.8** Accessible authentication (minimum) | AA | Logging in does not ask you to remember, copy or solve anything (password managers and paste work). | Your content |
| **3.3.9** Accessible authentication (enhanced) | AAA | No image recognition either («select the traffic lights»). | Your content |

## 4. Robust

| Criterion | Level | What it asks | State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **4.1.2** Name, role, value | A | Every control has a name, a role and a state that screen readers can read. | Meets |
| **4.1.3** Status messages | AA | Messages that appear without moving the focus are announced. | Meets |

The official text, in English: [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/). In Spanish: [the UNE-EN 301549 standard](https://www.une.org) and the guides of the [Observatorio de Accesibilidad](https://administracionelectronica.gob.es/pae_Home/pae_Estrategias/pae_Accesibilidad.html).

# Performance

How much GlassMarshmallow weighs and how to load only what you need. The tables are measured every time the
documentation is built, so they always match the current version.

## Size

What the browser downloads. Servers and CDNs (jsDelivr, unpkg, Cloudflare…) send it compressed, so the real
download is the **gzip** or **Brotli** column.

## Load only what you need

- **Link the `.min.css`** file in production; the other one has comments to read it.
- **The font is optional.** `glassmarshmallow-font.css` adds Montserrat; without it, the framework uses the
  system font and downloads nothing else. See [Typography](/docs/customize/typography).
- **Scripts go one by one.** Each component that moves has its own file and you only import the ones you use;
  pages with no menus, carousels or players need no JavaScript at all.
- **Arbitrary values** (`gm-mt-[1.75rem]`) are only written if you use them: `npx glassmarshmallow build` puts
  just those classes in a separate file.

## Glass and blur

The glass effect uses `backdrop-filter: blur()`, which the browser paints with the graphics card. A few glass
panels on a page are no problem, even on phones; dozens of large panels on top of each other, or blurring
something that moves (a video, an animation) under the glass, can make scrolling less smooth on older phones.
If you notice it, use a solid surface (`gm-bg-surface`) for the big panels and keep glass for the small ones.

## Animations

Most of the framework's animations only change `opacity` and `transform`, which do not make the browser
recalculate the layout. A few cost a little more: `gm-animate-blur-in` also animates `filter`, the shimmer and the
moving progress bar animate the background position, and the countdown animates the width. They all turn off on
their own with `prefers-reduced-motion`.

<!-- /docs/color/colors -->
# Palette

A palette of eight pastel colors, plus black, white and grays, used solid or glazed. This page lists them; the next pages of this section explain how to use them.

> **Accessibility:** every combination meets **WCAG 2.2 AA**, and most of them reach **AAA**. The details are at the end of the page.

## Palette

| Color | Name in the classes | Pastel | Text color (light mode) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sky | `sky` | `#5CDFEB` | `#02464B` |
| Blue | `blue` | `#8AB4FF` | `#003290` |
| Lavender | `lavender` | `#B9A3FF` | `#5F23B8` |
| Pink | `pink` | `#FFA6D1` | `#940061` |
| Peach | `peach` | `#FFB98A` | `#5F2E01` |
| Lemon | `lemon` | `#FFE38A` | `#4B3B01` |
| Mint | `mint` | `#8BE3B6` | `#014A2F` |
| Coral | `coral` | `#FF9B9B` | `#9C0226` |

In dark mode, the text color is the pastel itself.

## Black, white and grays

The same grays that the framework already uses, in a scale like Bootstrap's. They are used with the same classes as the pastels.

| Color | Value | Text on the solid color |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `white` | `#ffffff` | black |
| `gray-100` | `#f5f5f7` | black |
| `gray-200` | `#e8e8ed` | black |
| `gray-300` | `#d2d2d7` | black |
| `gray-400` | `#aeaeb2` | black |
| `gray-500` | `#8e8e93` | black |
| `gray-600` | `#636366` | white |
| `gray-700` | `#48484a` | white |
| `gray-800` | `#3a3a3c` | white |
| `gray-900` | `#1d1d1f` | white |
| `black` | `#000000` | white |

## Scales

Each color has 13 tones, from `025` (almost white) to `975` (almost black), calculated from its pastel: same hue, different lightness. The tone marked **★ pastel** is the pastel and **Aa text** is the text tone in light mode. Under each tone, its contrast on white (□) and on black (■): 4.5 or more is valid for text.

They are CSS variables, like Bootstrap's colors: `var(--gm-sky-500)`, `var(--gm-coral-800)`, `var(--gm-gray-050)`… There are no classes for each tone, so the file stays small.

## How to use them

Each color is used with these classes:

- [Colors](/docs/color/text): the text in a color, with `.gm-text-sky`.
- [Background](/docs/color/background): a solid background, with `.gm-bg-sky`.
- [Light and dark mode](/docs/color/color-modes): light or dark mode in one part of the page, with `data-theme`.
- [Theme](/docs/color/theme): solid, glazed or text in one go, with `.gm-theme-sky` and `.gm-theme-solid`, `.gm-theme-glass` or `.gm-theme-text`.

## CSS variables

Each color has three variables, so you can use it in your own CSS:

```css
--gm-sky: #5cdfeb;          /* the pastel */
--gm-sky-rgb: 92 223 235;   /* the same color in RGB channels, for transparency */
--gm-sky-text: #20747b;     /* the text tone (the pastel itself in dark mode) */
```

The glass values are variables too: `--gm-glass-alpha`, `--gm-glass-border-alpha`, `--gm-glass-radius`, `--gm-glass-blur` and `--gm-glass-shadow`.

## Accessibility

| Use | Contrast | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Black text on the solid color | 7.8:1 to 13.3:1 | AAA |
| Text on glass (light and dark) | about 14:1 | AAA |
| Colored text, dark mode | 9.7:1 to 16.6:1 | AAA |
| Colored text, light mode (tones 800 and 900) | 7:1 or more | AAA |
| Text on the grays (solid) | 7:1 or more, except `gray-500` (5.2:1) and `gray-600` (6:1) | AAA (those two, AA) |
| Gray text (`.gm-theme-text`) | 7:1 or more | AAA |

- **Never use white text on the solid pastel:** it stays below 2.2:1.
- The glass border is soft. Cards, alerts and buttons with text don't need more, but form controls that are recognized by their outline (fields, checkboxes, switches) use the framework's gray border, which reaches 3:1.
- Don't show a state with color alone: success, warning and error always come with an icon or a text.
- Glass lets the background show through. Over a photo or strong colors, measure the contrast of the text where you use it.

<!-- /docs/color/color-modes -->
# Light and dark mode

GlassMarshmallow has a light and a dark mode. You choose it with the `data-theme` attribute, on the whole page or on any part of it, like `data-bs-theme` in Bootstrap.

## The whole page

Put `data-theme` on `<html>`. Without it, the page is light.

```html
<html lang="en" data-theme="dark">
```

All the colors are CSS variables that change with the mode: page background, surfaces, text, lines, accent, the palette text tones and the glass. The browser's own parts (form controls and scrollbars) change too.

## One part of the page

Put `data-theme` on any element to change only that element and everything inside it. Add `.gm-bg-body` or `.gm-bg-surface` so that the area is painted with the background of its mode.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-3">
  <div data-theme="light" class="gm-bg-body gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">
    <b>Always light</b>
    <div class="gm-text-sky">.gm-text-sky</div>
    <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-glass gm-mt-2 gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-glass</div>
  </div>
  <div data-theme="dark" class="gm-bg-body gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">
    <b>Always dark</b>
    <div class="gm-text-sky">.gm-text-sky</div>
    <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-glass gm-mt-2 gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-glass</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Follow the system and remember the choice

The framework doesn't choose the mode for you. This script, in the `<head>` before the styles, uses the choice saved in the browser or, if there is none, the system preference. It runs before the page is painted, so it doesn't flash.

```html
<script>
  // Before the page is painted: the saved choice or, if there is none, the system preference
  (function () {
    var saved; try { saved = localStorage.getItem('theme'); } catch (e) {}
    var dark = saved === 'dark' || (saved !== 'light' && matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches);
    document.documentElement.dataset.theme = dark ? 'dark' : 'light';
  })();
</script>
```

To change the mode with a button, set `document.documentElement.dataset.theme` to `'light'` or `'dark'` and save it with `localStorage.setItem('theme', …)`.

## Accessibility

Every color of the framework is checked in both modes: text 4.5:1 or more (AA) and controls 3:1 or more.

<!-- /docs/color/text -->
# Colors

Change the color of the text with a class. Each color uses its text tone, which can be read in light and dark mode.

## Palette

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-2">
  <div class="gm-text-sky">.gm-text-sky</div>
  <div class="gm-text-blue">.gm-text-blue</div>
  <div class="gm-text-lavender">.gm-text-lavender</div>
  <div class="gm-text-pink">.gm-text-pink</div>
  <div class="gm-text-peach">.gm-text-peach</div>
  <div class="gm-text-lemon">.gm-text-lemon</div>
  <div class="gm-text-mint">.gm-text-mint</div>
  <div class="gm-text-coral">.gm-text-coral</div>
</div>
```

## Black, white and grays

Grays that would be too light to read in light mode use `gray-600`, and grays that would be too dark in dark mode use `gray-500`, so the text is always readable.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-2">
  <div class="gm-text-white">.gm-text-white</div>
  <div class="gm-text-gray-100">.gm-text-gray-100</div>
  <div class="gm-text-gray-200">.gm-text-gray-200</div>
  <div class="gm-text-gray-300">.gm-text-gray-300</div>
  <div class="gm-text-gray-400">.gm-text-gray-400</div>
  <div class="gm-text-gray-500">.gm-text-gray-500</div>
  <div class="gm-text-gray-600">.gm-text-gray-600</div>
  <div class="gm-text-gray-700">.gm-text-gray-700</div>
  <div class="gm-text-gray-800">.gm-text-gray-800</div>
  <div class="gm-text-gray-900">.gm-text-gray-900</div>
  <div class="gm-text-black">.gm-text-black</div>
</div>
```

## Page text

The three text colors of the interface, which change with light and dark mode.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-2">
  <div class="gm-text-body">.gm-text-body</div>
  <div class="gm-text-secondary">.gm-text-secondary</div>
  <div class="gm-text-muted">.gm-text-muted</div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- Every `.gm-text-*` class reaches at least 4.5:1 on the page background (AA).
- Don't use color alone to give meaning: add a word or an icon.

<!-- /docs/color/background -->
# Background

Paint the background of any element with a class. Unlike Bootstrap, each background class also sets the text color that can be read on it, so the result always meets AA.

## Palette

The solid pastel, with black text in light and dark mode.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-2">
  <div class="gm-bg-sky gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-sky</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-blue gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-blue</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-lavender gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-lavender</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-pink gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-pink</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-peach gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-peach</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-lemon gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-lemon</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-mint gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-mint</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-coral gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-coral</div>
</div>
```

## Black, white and grays

Black text up to `gray-500` and white text from `gray-600`.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-2">
  <div class="gm-bg-white gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-white</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-gray-100 gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-gray-100</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-gray-200 gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-gray-200</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-gray-300 gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-gray-300</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-gray-400 gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-gray-400</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-gray-500 gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-gray-500</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-gray-600 gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-gray-600</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-gray-700 gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-gray-700</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-gray-800 gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-gray-800</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-gray-900 gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-gray-900</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-black gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-black</div>
</div>
```

The scales also include `gray-025`, `gray-050`, `gray-950` and `gray-975` (`.gm-bg-gray-025`…).

## Interface backgrounds

They follow light and dark mode: the page background, the background of cards and panels, and no background.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-2">
  <div class="gm-bg-body gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-body</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-surface gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-surface</div>
  <div class="gm-bg-transparent gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-bg-transparent</div>
</div>
```

## Glazed background

For the glazed version, use the [Theme](/docs/color/theme) classes: `.gm-theme-sky .gm-theme-glass`.

<!-- /docs/color/color-scheme -->
# Color scheme

Set the color scheme of a single element, so the browser paints its own parts to match: native form controls, scrollbars and the background of an `<iframe>`.

| Class | Styles |
| --- | --- |
| `.gm-color-scheme-light` | `color-scheme: light;` |
| `.gm-color-scheme-dark` | `color-scheme: dark;` |
| `.gm-color-scheme-auto` | `color-scheme: light dark;` |

GlassMarshmallow already sets it for you: `data-theme="light"` and `data-theme="dark"` set the matching scheme. Use these classes only when one element must use a different scheme than the area around it.

## Light and dark

Add `.gm-color-scheme-light` or `.gm-color-scheme-dark` to the element that needs it, not to a wrapper. In the example, the second field keeps the light browser parts inside a dark area.

```html-code
<div data-theme="dark">
  <!-- The browser paints this field and its picker in dark mode -->
  <select>…</select>
  <!-- …and this one in light mode -->
  <select class="gm-color-scheme-light">…</select>
</div>
```

These classes only change the parts the browser paints. They don't change the framework colors: to put an area in light or dark mode, use `data-theme` (see [Light and dark mode](/docs/color/color-modes)).

## Follow the system preference

`.gm-color-scheme-auto` lets the browser follow the system preference for that element, even if the page forces a mode.

```html
<iframe class="gm-color-scheme-auto" src="..."></iframe>
```

## Embedded content

An embedded document can't see the `data-theme` of your page. If an embed has no dark mode, the browser may paint a white background behind it when the system is dark. Add `.gm-color-scheme-light` to that `<iframe>` only.

```html
<iframe class="gm-color-scheme-light" src="..."></iframe>
```

<!-- /docs/color/theme -->
# Theme

Combine a color class with a use class to set the background, text and border of any element in one go, like Bootstrap's theme utilities.

## How it works

1. **The color:** `.gm-theme-sky`, `.gm-theme-blue`, `.gm-theme-lavender`, `.gm-theme-pink`, `.gm-theme-peach`, `.gm-theme-lemon`, `.gm-theme-mint` or `.gm-theme-coral`.
2. **The use:** `.gm-theme-solid`, `.gm-theme-glass` or `.gm-theme-text`.

The black, white and gray classes work the same way: `.gm-theme-white`, `.gm-theme-gray-100` to `.gm-theme-gray-900` and `.gm-theme-black`.

## Pink and blue

`.gm-theme-pink-blue` is **pink by day and blue at night**: the color we use for examples and for what should stand out (like the “For agents” button on the home page). It combines with the same uses and also exists as a variable: `--gm-pink-blue`.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-gap-3 gm-flex-wrap">
  <div class="gm-theme-pink-blue gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-pink-blue .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-pink-blue gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-pink-blue .gm-theme-glass</div>
</div>
```

Switch between light and dark mode to see it turn from pink to blue.

## Turquoise accent at night

With `class="gm-accent-turquoise"` on `<html>`, the night accent color is turquoise (`#1cabb0`, 7.4:1 on black) instead of blue; by day it stays pink. It changes focus, fields, selection, accordion icons and accent buttons.

```html
<html lang="en" class="gm-accent-turquoise" data-theme="dark">
```

## Solid

`.gm-theme-solid` paints the pastel as the background, with black text in both light and dark mode.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-3">
  <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-sky .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-blue gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-blue .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-lavender gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-lavender .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-pink gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-pink .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-peach gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-peach .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-lemon gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-lemon .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-mint gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-mint .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-coral gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-coral .gm-theme-solid</div>
</div>
```

With grays, the text is black up to `gray-500` and white from `gray-600`:

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-3">
  <div class="gm-theme-white gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-white .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-100 gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-gray-100 .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-200 gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-gray-200 .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-300 gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-gray-300 .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-400 gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-gray-400 .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-500 gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-gray-500 .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-600 gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-gray-600 .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-700 gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-gray-700 .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-800 gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-gray-800 .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-900 gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-gray-900 .gm-theme-solid</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-black gm-theme-solid gm-py-3 gm-px-4 gm-rounded-sm">.gm-theme-black .gm-theme-solid</div>
</div>
```

## Glass

`.gm-theme-glass` is the glazed version: the color at 18 % over whatever is behind it, a 1 px border at 41 %, a 7 px blur, 21 px corners and a soft shadow. The text keeps the page color.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-3">
  <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-sky .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-blue gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-blue .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-lavender gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-lavender .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-pink gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-pink .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-peach gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-peach .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-lemon gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-lemon .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-mint gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-mint .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-coral gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-coral .gm-theme-glass</div>
</div>
```

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-3">
  <div class="gm-theme-white gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-white .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-100 gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-gray-100 .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-200 gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-gray-200 .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-300 gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-gray-300 .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-400 gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-gray-400 .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-500 gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-gray-500 .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-600 gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-gray-600 .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-700 gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-gray-700 .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-800 gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-gray-800 .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-gray-900 gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-gray-900 .gm-theme-glass</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-black gm-theme-glass gm-py-3 gm-px-4">.gm-theme-black .gm-theme-glass</div>
</div>
```

## Colored text

`.gm-theme-text` writes the text in the color of the palette, in a darker tone so it can be read on the light background.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-3">
  <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-text">.gm-theme-sky .gm-theme-text</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-blue gm-theme-text">.gm-theme-blue .gm-theme-text</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-lavender gm-theme-text">.gm-theme-lavender .gm-theme-text</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-pink gm-theme-text">.gm-theme-pink .gm-theme-text</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-peach gm-theme-text">.gm-theme-peach .gm-theme-text</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-lemon gm-theme-text">.gm-theme-lemon .gm-theme-text</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-mint gm-theme-text">.gm-theme-mint .gm-theme-text</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-coral gm-theme-text">.gm-theme-coral .gm-theme-text</div>
</div>
```

<!-- /docs/customize/typography -->
# Typography

GlassMarshmallow uses **Montserrat** for all text and the system monospace font for code.

## Fonts

| Variable | Value | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--gm-font` | Montserrat (if it does not load: the system font) | All text |
| `--gm-font-mono` | `ui-monospace`, SF Mono, Menlo | Code |

Montserrat comes with the framework, in a separate, **optional** file: `glassmarshmallow-font.css`. It is served from your own site, without Google Fonts: a single 35 KB file with every weight (300–800) and the Latin characters. Add it next to the framework CSS and preload the font in the `<head>`, so it arrives before the page is first painted. If it does not make it in time on a slow connection, that visit uses a fallback font with the same measurements (adjusted Arial) and the text does not jump while loading:

```html-code
<link rel="preload" href="node_modules/glassmarshmallow/dist/fonts/montserrat-latin.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow-font.min.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/glassmarshmallow/dist/css/glassmarshmallow.min.css">
```

The CSS looks for the font in `../fonts/`: if you copy the files into your project, keep the `css` and `fonts` folders side by side. Montserrat is licensed under the [SIL Open Font License](https://openfontlicense.org) (in `fonts/OFL.txt`): free to use, commercial projects included.

## Sizes

| Element | Size | Weight | Details |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `h1` | 2.3 to 3.2 rem (grows with the screen) | 700 | Very tight letters (−0.055 em), line height 1.1 |
| `h2` | browser default (1.5 rem) | 700 | Tight letters (−0.025 em) |
| `h3` | browser default (1.17 rem) | 700 | |
| Text | 1 rem (16 px) | 400 | Line height 1.5 |
| `.gm-small` | 0.84 rem | 400 | |
| `.gm-eyebrow` | 0.9 rem | 600 | Gray |
| Buttons | 1 rem (`--sm`: 0.84 rem) | 650 | |
| Code | 0.86 rem | 400 | Monospace |

On the home page, `h1` and `h2` headings switch to weight 800.

## Changing the font

Do not add `glassmarshmallow-font.css` (so Montserrat is not downloaded) and change the variable. If you use another font, check that it reads well and the design does not break (Montserrat is wide: others may leave more space).

```html-code
<style>
  :root { --gm-font: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif; }
</style>
```

## Accessibility

- Sizes are in `rem`: if the person enlarges text in their browser, everything grows with it (WCAG 1.4.4).
- Line height of 1.5 for text and lines of 80 characters at most (WCAG 1.4.8 and 1.4.12).
- Text is not justified: gaps between words make reading harder.

<!-- /docs/customize/background -->
# Page background

The page background color comes from a variable that changes on its own with light and dark mode.

## Colors

| Variable | Light | Dark | For |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--gm-bg` | `#f5f5f7` | `#000` | Page background |
| `--gm-surface` | white at 82 % | dark gray at 82 % | Glass cards and panels |
| `--gm-surface-solid` | `#fff` | `#1c1c1e` | Opaque panels (menus, windows) |

The very light gray by day and black at night is the framework background: white cards (or gray at night) stand out on it without strong borders.

## Changing the background

Change the variable in both modes:

```html-code
<style>
  :root { --gm-bg: #fbfaf7; }
  [data-theme="dark"] { --gm-bg: #0b0b0c; }
</style>
```

Then check the text contrast on the new background: regular text needs 4.5:1 (7:1 for AAA), and so does the secondary gray.

## Home page lights

This site's home page uses its own background with colored lights, a dot grid and, at night, the old TV effect. That background belongs to the site, not the framework. Its effects (the TV one and those to come) will be in **Tools › Effects**, to generate and copy them.

<!-- /docs/layout/containers -->
# Containers

The container centers the page content and leaves a margin on the sides. It is the first thing inside each section.

## Container

`.gm-container` is at most 1240 px wide and leaves 24 px on each side (16 px on phones).

```html
<div class="gm-container gm-py-4" style="outline: 2px dashed var(--gm-field-border)">
  Centered content, with a margin on the sides.
</div>
```

## Narrow

`.gm-container--narrow`, at most 960 px: for long texts, forms or articles, which read better without very long lines.

```html
<div class="gm-container gm-container--narrow gm-py-4" style="outline: 2px dashed var(--gm-field-border)">
  Comfortable to read.
</div>
```

## Full width

`.gm-container--fluid` reaches the edges of the screen but keeps the side margin.

```html
<div class="gm-container--fluid gm-py-4" style="outline: 2px dashed var(--gm-field-border)">
  Edge to edge.
</div>
```

## Inner page

`gm-page` leaves the top space of the pages that are not the home page (4.5 rem) and `gm-lead` is the lead paragraph below the title: a bit bigger and in a comfortable reading column (42.5 rem).

```html
<section class="gm-container gm-page gm-pt-0">
  <h1>Icons</h1>
  <p class="gm-lead gm-muted gm-mb-0">More than 300 free icons, outline and filled, with the same names as Bootstrap Icons.</p>
</section>
```

In the example, `gm-pt-0` removes the top space so it fits in the box.

## Changing the width

The maximum width is the `--gm-container` variable. Change it for the whole site or only inside a section:

```html-code
<style>
  :root { --gm-container: 1100px; }
</style>
```

| Class | Max width | Side margin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.gm-container` | 1240 px (`--gm-container`) | 24 px; 16 px up to 600 px |
| `.gm-container--narrow` | 960 px | same |
| `.gm-container--fluid` | full | same |

<!-- /docs/layout/sections -->
# Sections

Each part of a home page (About me, Skills, Contact…) is a section: some space above and below, the title centered and the text below it, in a narrow container so lines are not too long.

## Example

```html
<section class="gm-section gm-py-10">
  <div class="gm-container gm-container--narrow">
    <h2 class="gm-section__title">About me</h2>
    <p class="gm-section__text">Hi, I am <strong>Sara Paez Yamuza</strong> and I am a web developer. I like working on both sides of an application: what you see and what is behind it.</p>
    <p class="gm-section__text">I love taking part in projects from the idea until they are up and running.</p>
  </div>
</section>
```

## Where each thing goes

| Piece | Class | How it looks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The section | `.gm-section` | 6 rem above and below (3.5 rem on phones) |
| The width | `.gm-container .gm-container--narrow` | Centered, 960 px at most; text, 80 characters per line at most |
| The title | `.gm-section__title` | Centered, 2 rem (1.7 rem on phones), with 2 rem below |
| The text | `.gm-section__text` | In a centered column of 44 rem at most, left-aligned, 1.1 rem with 1.7 line height, in gray; highlighted words (`<strong>`) in the text color |

## With another piece below

Any component can go after the title, for example an [accordion](/docs/components/accordion):

```html
<section class="gm-section gm-py-10">
  <div class="gm-container gm-container--narrow">
    <h2 class="gm-section__title">Skills</h2>
    <div class="gm-accordion">
      <details class="gm-accordion__item" name="section-example">
        <summary class="gm-accordion__summary">
          <span class="gm-accordion__icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="gmi gmi-palette"></i></span>
          <span class="gm-accordion__text"><span class="gm-accordion__title">Design</span><span class="gm-accordion__meta">3 tools</span></span>
          <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-down gm-accordion__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
        </summary>
        <div class="gm-accordion__content"><ul class="gm-accordion__list"><li>Figma</li><li>Photoshop</li><li>Illustrator</li></ul></div>
      </details>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

## Accessibility

- Each section starts with its title (`h2`) and titles go in order, without skipping levels.
- Text is left-aligned: centered, long paragraphs are hard to read (WCAG 1.4.8).
- Lines of 80 characters at most and 1.7 line height (WCAG 1.4.8 and 1.4.12).
- The gray text reaches 7:1 on the background (AAA).

<!-- /docs/layout/page -->
# Page structure

The header, the content and the footer, with the footer at the bottom of the window even when the page is short. It is this site's structure.

## Example

```html-code
<body class="gm-app">
  <a class="gm-skip-link" href="#content">Skip to content</a>
  <header>…</header>
  <main id="content" class="gm-app__main" tabindex="-1">…</main>
  <div class="gm-app__end" aria-hidden="true"></div>
  <footer class="gm-site-footer">…</footer>
</body>
```

`gm-app__end` takes the free space: if the page is short, it grows and the footer stays at the bottom of the window with no scroll; if it is long, it is as small as possible.

## Centered content

`gm-app__main--center` centers the content in height in the gap between the header and the footer (this site's home page).

## Fade down to the footer

With the [lights background](/docs/customize/background) (`.gm-backdrop`), `gm-app__end--fade` adds a gradient that rises behind the end of the content to the footer color: white in light mode and black in dark mode. It starts and ends smoothly, with no step.

```html-code
<main id="content" class="gm-app__main gm-app__main--center" tabindex="-1">…</main>
<div class="gm-app__end gm-app__end--fade" aria-hidden="true"></div>
```

## Accessibility

- `tabindex="-1"` on `main` lets the [skip link](/docs/helpers/skip-link) move the focus to the content.
- `gm-app__end` is empty and decorative: `aria-hidden="true"`.

<!-- /docs/layout/breakpoints -->
# Breakpoints

The screen widths where the layout changes. You think of phones first and add from each breakpoint upwards, as in Bootstrap.

| Name | From | Screens | Class example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| (no prefix) | 0 | phones | `gm-col-12` |
| `sm` | 600 px | large phones and landscape | `gm-sm-col-6` |
| `md` | 860 px | tablets; from here, the desktop navigation bar | `gm-md-col-4` |
| `lg` | 1100 px | computers | `gm-lg-col-3` |
| `xl` | 1300 px | large screens | `gm-xl-col-2` |

## How to use them

A prefixed class applies **from** that width upwards. Without a prefix, everywhere. Here, one column on phones, two from `sm` and four from `lg` (resize the window to see it):

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-sm">
  <div class="gm-sm-col-6 gm-lg-col-3 gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">1</div>
  <div class="gm-sm-col-6 gm-lg-col-3 gm-theme-pink-blue gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">2</div>
  <div class="gm-sm-col-6 gm-lg-col-3 gm-theme-mint gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">3</div>
  <div class="gm-sm-col-6 gm-lg-col-3 gm-theme-peach gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">4</div>
</div>
```

## In your own CSS

In `@media` you have to write the number (CSS variables do not work there). Use the same values, from phones upwards:

```css
.my-block { padding: 16px; }

@media (min-width: 860px) {
  .my-block { padding: 32px; }
}
```

From JavaScript, the values are in variables: `--gm-breakpoint-sm`, `--gm-breakpoint-md`, `--gm-breakpoint-lg` and `--gm-breakpoint-xl`.

```js
const md = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--gm-breakpoint-md'); // '860px'
const tablet = matchMedia(`(min-width: ${md})`).matches;
```

<!-- /docs/layout/grid -->
# Grid

To place pieces in columns. It has 12 columns, like Bootstrap's, but is built with CSS Grid: each child says how many of the 12 it spans, and that can change at each [breakpoint](/docs/layout/breakpoints).

## Columns

`.gm-grid` on the container and `.gm-col-N` on each child (N from 1 to 12). Without a column class, the child spans the whole row.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-sm">
  <div class="gm-col-8 gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">8 of 12</div>
  <div class="gm-col-4 gm-theme-pink-blue gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">4 of 12</div>
  <div class="gm-col-4 gm-theme-mint gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">4</div>
  <div class="gm-col-4 gm-theme-mint gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">4</div>
  <div class="gm-col-4 gm-theme-mint gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">4</div>
</div>
```

## By screen width

With a prefix (`sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`), the column changes from that width. Here: stacked on phones, two from `md` and three from `lg`.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-sm">
  <div class="gm-md-col-6 gm-lg-col-4 gm-theme-lavender gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">A</div>
  <div class="gm-md-col-6 gm-lg-col-4 gm-theme-pink gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">B</div>
  <div class="gm-md-col-12 gm-lg-col-4 gm-theme-peach gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">C</div>
</div>
```

## Equal columns

Without counting: `.gm-cols-2`, `-3`, `-4` or `-6` split the space into equal columns. Also with a prefix.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-cols-1 gm-sm-cols-2 gm-lg-cols-4 gm-gap-sm">
  <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">1</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">2</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">3</div>
  <div class="gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">4</div>
</div>
```

## As many as fit

`.gm-grid--auto` fits as many columns of at least 240 px as there is room for, with no breakpoints. Ideal for cards. Change the minimum with `--gm-grid-min`.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-grid--auto gm-gap-sm" style="--gm-grid-min: 10rem">
  <div class="gm-card">One</div>
  <div class="gm-card">Two</div>
  <div class="gm-card">Three</div>
  <div class="gm-card">Four</div>
  <div class="gm-card">Five</div>
</div>
```

## Offset

`.gm-offset-N` leaves N empty columns before the child. For example, to center a 6-column block:

```html
<div class="gm-grid">
  <div class="gm-col-12 gm-md-col-6 gm-md-offset-3 gm-theme-lemon gm-theme-solid gm-p-4 gm-rounded-sm">Centered from md</div>
</div>
```

## Spacing

The gap between columns is 1.5 rem. Change it with the usual [spacing](/docs/utilities/spacing), `gm-gap-0` … `gm-gap-16` (the same scale as margins and padding), or with the `--gm-gap` variable. `gm-gap-sm` and `gm-gap-lg` still work: they are `gm-gap-3` and `gm-gap-10`.

## To build with (like Tailwind)
