```html
      <option>Web application</option>
      <option>Website maintenance</option>
      <option>Other</option>
    </select>
  </div>

  <fieldset class="gm-field">
    <legend>What is your ideal timeline? (optional)</legend>
    <div class="gm-check">
      <label><input type="checkbox" name="timeline"> Urgent (within 1 month)</label>
      <label><input type="checkbox" name="timeline"> 1 to 2 months</label>
      <label><input type="checkbox" name="timeline"> 2 to 3 months</label>
      <label><input type="checkbox" name="timeline"> Flexible, no strict deadline</label>
    </div>
  </fieldset>

  <fieldset class="gm-field" aria-describedby="contact-site-help">
    <legend>Do you already have a domain or website? (required)</legend>
    <p class="gm-field__help" id="contact-site-help">Mark «Yes» if you already own a domain or a published website.</p>
    <div class="gm-check">
      <label><input type="radio" name="has-site" value="yes" required> Yes</label>
      <label><input type="radio" name="has-site" value="no"> No</label>
    </div>
  </fieldset>

  <div class="gm-field">
    <label for="contact-details">Anything else I should know? (required)</label>
    <p class="gm-field__help" id="contact-details-help">Tell me about the project you have in mind.</p>
    <textarea id="contact-details" name="details" rows="5" aria-describedby="contact-details-help" required></textarea>
  </div>

  <div class="gm-form__actions">
    <button type="submit" class="gm-btn gm-btn--accent">Send</button>
    <button type="reset" class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary">Reset</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

## Pieces

| Class | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.gm-form` | The glass panel of the form |
| `.gm-field` | A label with its field (or a `fieldset` with its options) |
| `.gm-field__help` | Help text, linked with `aria-describedby` |
| `.gm-field__error` | Error message |
| `.gm-input-group` | Two fields in a row: a third and two thirds (prefix and number) |
| `.gm-check` | A list of checkboxes or radio buttons |
| `.gm-form__actions` | The buttons at the end |
| `.gm-btn--accent` | The accent button (pink by day, blue at night) to send |

## Errors

Mark the field with `aria-invalid="true"` and link the message with `aria-describedby`. The message says what to do, not just that something is wrong.

```html
<div class="gm-field">
  <label for="err-email">Email (required)</label>
  <input id="err-email" type="email" value="sara@" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="err-email-msg">
  <p class="gm-field__error" id="err-email-msg">Write a complete email, for example sara@example.com.</p>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- Every field has a visible label. Groups of checkboxes or radio buttons go in a `fieldset` with its `legend`.
- Field borders reach 3.5:1 in light mode and 3.9:1 in dark mode (3:1 is required).
- While you type, the field shows a ring and a pink border by day and blue at night (5.5:1 in light, 8:1 in dark; 3:1 is required for borders).
- Use `autocomplete` (name, email, tel…) so browsers can fill the form.
- Write “(required)” in the label of required fields, as well as `required`, and “(optional)” in the label of optional ones. More in [Form rules](/docs/forms/rules).
- The send button: white text on dark pink (8.6:1) by day and dark blue (11.3:1) at night, AAA.

<!-- /docs/forms/segmented -->
# Segmented control

Options together in a gray bar; the chosen one sits in a white pill (black at night) with a shadow.

## To pick a setting

With radio buttons inside a `fieldset` with its `legend`. The radio circle is hidden: the white pill shows which one is chosen. It changes with the mouse or the arrow keys.

```html
<fieldset class="gm-field">
  <legend>Preview</legend>
  <div class="gm-segmented">
    <label><input type="radio" name="example-view" checked> Light mode</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="example-view"> Dark mode</label>
  </div>
</fieldset>
```

## To filter, with a count

With buttons that say whether they are pressed (`aria-pressed`), inside a named group. Each option can show how many items there are (`.gm-segmented__count`).

```html
<div class="gm-segmented" role="group" aria-label="Filter by type">
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">All</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="true">Books <span class="gm-segmented__count">3</span></button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">Manga <span class="gm-segmented__count">20</span></button>
</div>
```

## Stacked

With more than 3 options or long labels, one below the other: `.gm-segmented--stack`.

```html
<fieldset class="gm-field">
  <legend>Harmony</legend>
  <div class="gm-segmented gm-segmented--stack">
    <label><input type="radio" name="example-harmony"> Monochromatic</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="example-harmony" checked> Analogous</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="example-harmony"> Complementary</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="example-harmony"> Triadic</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="example-harmony"> Split complementary</label>
  </div>
</fieldset>
```

## Small

`.gm-segmented--small`, for toolbars or tight spaces.

```html
<div class="gm-segmented gm-segmented--small" role="group" aria-label="Sort">
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="true">Recent</button>
  <button type="button" aria-pressed="false">A-Z</button>
</div>
```

## When to use it

- **2 or 3 short options**, in a row.
- **More than 3 or long labels**, stacked (`--stack`).
- For settings applied right away (view, filter, sort). In a form to submit, radios work too.

## Accessibility

- With radios: the `fieldset` and its `legend` say what is being chosen, and it works like any group of options (Tab to enter, arrows to change).
- With buttons: `role="group"` and `aria-label` on the bar, and `aria-pressed` on each button.
- The gray text reaches 7.5:1 by day and 7.1:1 at night on the bar (AAA); the chosen one, regular text.
- Each option is 34 px tall, but the touch area reaches 44 px (WCAG 2.5.5).
- The chosen one stands out by the pill and the shadow, not just color.

<!-- /docs/forms/range -->
# Range

To pick a number in a range by dragging: volume, opacity, size… The thumb is a round dot and the filled part uses the accent color.

## Example

```html
<div class="gm-field gm-max-w-md">
  <label for="example-volume">Volume</label>
  <input id="example-volume" class="gm-range" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="40">
</div>
```

## With the value shown

Show the value next to the label with an `<output>`. That way the exact number is known without guessing from the position.

```html
<div class="gm-field gm-max-w-md">
  <div class="gm-flex gm-justify-between gm-items-baseline">
    <label class="gm-font-bold" for="example-opacity">Opacity</label>
    <output id="example-opacity-value" for="example-opacity" class="gm-muted">70 %</output>
  </div>
  <input id="example-opacity" class="gm-range" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="70" oninput="document.getElementById('example-opacity-value').textContent = this.value + ' %'">
</div>
```

## Name and value on one line

`gm-slider` puts the name on the left, the value on the right (with equal-width digits, so it does not jump while moving) and the bar below. It is the one in this site's generators. `gm-slider__help` adds a hint below.

```html
<div class="gm-slider gm-max-w-md">
  <label for="example-blur">Blur</label>
  <output id="example-blur-value" for="example-blur">12 px</output>
  <input id="example-blur" class="gm-range" type="range" min="0" max="40" value="12" oninput="document.getElementById('example-blur-value').textContent = this.value + ' px'">
  <p class="gm-slider__help gm-muted gm-m-0">How much whatever is behind the glass is blurred.</p>
</div>
```

## Disabled

```html
<div class="gm-field gm-max-w-md">
  <label for="example-disabled">Brightness</label>
  <input id="example-disabled" class="gm-range" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50" disabled>
</div>
```

## Script

Firefox paints the filled part on its own. Chrome and Safari do not: the optional script puts the value's percentage in `--gm-range-progress` every time the bar moves. Without the script the bar works the same, but all in gray.

```html
<script type="module">
  import { initRanges, updateRange } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/range.js';
  initRanges();

  // If you change the value from your code, repaint it:
  const volume = document.querySelector('#volume');
  volume.value = 80;
  updateRange(volume);
</script>
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ← → / ↑ ↓ | One step (`step`) down or up |
| Page Up / Page Down | 10 % up or down |
| Home / End | To the minimum or maximum |

## Accessibility

- It is a real `<input type="range">` with its `<label>`: screen readers say the name and the value.
- If the bare number is unclear (“70”), add `aria-valuetext` with the value in words (“70 percent”).
- The dot is white with a 3.5:1 gray border, so it shows on white and dark backgrounds (WCAG 1.4.11). With the keyboard it gets a focus ring.
- The bar is 44 px tall so it is easy to press (WCAG 2.5.5, AAA), even though the visible line is thin.
- Dragging is not the only way: it also works with the keyboard or by clicking on the bar (WCAG 2.5.7).

<!-- /docs/forms/date-picker -->
# Date picker

A calendar with a glass panel, the month in large type and the days in 44 px circles. Today is in blue and the chosen day is filled.

## Example

Add `data-gm-calendar` and load the calendar script: it creates the calendar, changes the month and lets you choose a day with the mouse or the keyboard.

```html
<div class="gm-calendar" data-gm-calendar data-today="2026-10-17" data-selected="2026-10-22"></div>

<script type="module">
  import { initCalendars } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/calendar.js';
  initCalendars();
</script>
```


## Days

| Day | How to mark it | How it looks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Today | `aria-current="date"` | Blue and bold |
| Chosen | `aria-pressed="true"` | Black circle in light mode, white in dark mode |
| From another month | `.is-outside` | Gray |
| Not available | `disabled` | Paler, and it cannot be chosen |

## Options

| Attribute | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `data-selected="2026-10-22"` | The chosen day |
| `data-month="2026-10"` | The month shown at the start |
| `data-today="2026-10-17"` | Which day is «today» (by default, the date of the device) |
| `data-locale="es"` | Language of the names (by default, the `lang` of the page) |
| `data-min`, `data-max` | First and last day that can be chosen |

When a day is chosen, the calendar sends the `gm-date-change` event with the date:

```js
document.querySelector('.gm-calendar').addEventListener('gm-date-change', (event) => {
  console.log(event.detail.date); // '2026-10-22'
});
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ← → | Previous or next day |
| ↑ ↓ | Same day of the previous or next week |
| Home / End | First or last day of the week |
| Page Up / Page Down | Previous or next month |
| Enter / Space | Choose the day |

## Only with CSS

Without the script you can write the calendar by hand: the framework gives the look and your page decides what happens.

```html-code
<div class="gm-calendar" role="group" aria-labelledby="cal-title">
  <div class="gm-calendar__header">
    <h3 class="gm-calendar__title" id="cal-title">October <span>2026</span></h3>
    <div class="gm-calendar__nav">
      <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Previous month"><i class="gmi gmi-chevron-left" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
      <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Next month"><i class="gmi gmi-chevron-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <table class="gm-calendar__grid">
    <thead><tr><th scope="col"><abbr title="Monday">Mon</abbr></th><th scope="col"><abbr title="Tuesday">Tue</abbr></th><th scope="col"><abbr title="Wednesday">Wed</abbr></th><th scope="col"><abbr title="Thursday">Thu</abbr></th><th scope="col"><abbr title="Friday">Fri</abbr></th><th scope="col"><abbr title="Saturday">Sat</abbr></th><th scope="col"><abbr title="Sunday">Sun</abbr></th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
        <tr><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day is-outside" aria-label="September 28, 2026">28</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day is-outside" aria-label="September 29, 2026">29</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day is-outside" aria-label="September 30, 2026">30</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 1, 2026">1</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 2, 2026">2</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 3, 2026">3</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 4, 2026">4</button></td></tr>
        <tr><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 5, 2026">5</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 6, 2026">6</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 7, 2026">7</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 8, 2026">8</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 9, 2026">9</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 10, 2026">10</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 11, 2026">11</button></td></tr>
        <tr><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 12, 2026">12</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 13, 2026">13</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 14, 2026">14</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 15, 2026">15</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 16, 2026">16</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 17, 2026" aria-current="date">17</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 18, 2026">18</button></td></tr>
        <tr><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 19, 2026">19</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 20, 2026">20</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 21, 2026">21</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 22, 2026" aria-pressed="true">22</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 23, 2026">23</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 24, 2026">24</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 25, 2026">25</button></td></tr>
        <tr><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 26, 2026">26</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 27, 2026">27</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 28, 2026">28</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 29, 2026">29</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 30, 2026">30</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day" aria-label="October 31, 2026">31</button></td><td><button type="button" class="gm-calendar__day is-outside" aria-label="November 1, 2026">1</button></td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- Each day is a button with the full date in `aria-label`, so screen readers say «October 22, 2026» and not just «22».
- The days of the week use `<abbr>` with the full name.
- The month buttons have `aria-label`.
- Days of 44 px, the size WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA) asks for, also on mobile.
- Contrast: numbers 15:1 or more, today in blue 5:1 or more, days from other months 5:1 or more (AA).

<!-- /docs/forms/color-picker -->
# Color picker

A button with the color swatch that opens a window to choose it: color wheel, hue, saturation, lightness and opacity bars, the color code and the contrast of white and black text on top. It is the one used by the tools on this site.

## Example

Press the button to open the window.

```html
<div class="gm-color-picker" data-gm-color-picker data-label="Background color">
  <input type="hidden" name="background" value="#5cdfeb" />
</div>
```

## Without opacity

With `data-alpha="false"` the opacity bar goes away and the color is always opaque.

```html
<div class="gm-color-picker" data-gm-color-picker data-label="Text color" data-alpha="false">
  <input type="hidden" name="text" value="#004b96" />
</div>
```

## Script

The framework provides the look. The optional script builds the button and the window, and stores the color in the `<input>`:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { initColorPickers } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/color-picker.js';
  initColorPickers();
</script>
```

- The chosen color goes into the `<input>`'s `value` (`#rrggbb`, or `rgba()` with transparency), so it is sent with the form.
- Every change fires `input` and `change` on the `<input>`, and `gm-color-change` on the picker with the color in `detail.value`.
- Texts are in Spanish if the page has `<html lang="es">`, and in English otherwise. They can be changed with `initColorPickers(document, { texts: { done: 'OK' } })`.

```js
document.querySelector('.gm-color-picker').addEventListener('gm-color-change', (event) => {
  document.body.style.background = event.detail.value;
});
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Opens the window (on the button) |
| ← → | On the wheel: changes the hue (with Shift, 10 at a time) |
| ↑ ↓ | On the wheel: changes the saturation |
| ← → on a bar | Moves the bar |
| Escape | Closes the window and focus returns to the button |

## Accessibility

- The window is a `<dialog>` with a title; when it closes, focus returns to the button.
- The wheel is a `slider` that states hue and saturation in words (“Hue 186 degrees, saturation 79 %”).
- The bars are `<input type="range">` with their `<label>` and value; the thumb is a round dot.
- If the typed code is not valid, the field says so in text, not just with color.
- The white and black text contrast helps choose colors that read well (WCAG 1.4.3).

<!-- /docs/components/accordion -->
# Accordion

A list of sections that open and close, all in one glass card and separated by a thin line.

## Example

With the same `name` on every `<details>`, only one opens at a time.

```html
<div class="gm-accordion">
  <details class="gm-accordion__item" name="questions">
    <summary class="gm-accordion__summary">
      <span class="gm-accordion__title">How long does shipping take?</span>
      <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-down gm-accordion__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    </summary>
    <div class="gm-accordion__content">
      <p>Between 2 and 4 working days on the mainland. To the islands, between 4 and 7.</p>
    </div>
  </details>
  <details class="gm-accordion__item" name="questions">
    <summary class="gm-accordion__summary">
      <span class="gm-accordion__title">Can I return an order?</span>
      <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-down gm-accordion__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    </summary>
    <div class="gm-accordion__content">
      <p>Yes, within 30 days of receiving it, no questions asked.</p>
    </div>
  </details>
  <details class="gm-accordion__item" name="questions">
    <summary class="gm-accordion__summary">
      <span class="gm-accordion__title">Which payment methods do you accept?</span>
      <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-down gm-accordion__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    </summary>
    <div class="gm-accordion__content">
      <ul class="gm-accordion__list">
        <li>Card</li>
        <li>Bank transfer</li>
        <li>Bizum</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </details>
</div>
```

## With icon and detail

An icon in a circle on the left and a detail line under the title.

```html
<div class="gm-accordion">
  <details class="gm-accordion__item" name="skills" open>
    <summary class="gm-accordion__summary">
      <span class="gm-accordion__icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="gmi gmi-palette"></i></span>
      <span class="gm-accordion__text">
        <span class="gm-accordion__title">Design</span>
        <span class="gm-accordion__meta">4 tools</span>
      </span>
      <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-down gm-accordion__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    </summary>
    <div class="gm-accordion__content">
      <ul class="gm-accordion__list">
        <li>Figma</li>
        <li>Clip Studio Paint</li>
        <li>Photoshop</li>
        <li>Illustrator</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </details>
  <details class="gm-accordion__item" name="skills">
    <summary class="gm-accordion__summary">
      <span class="gm-accordion__icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="gmi gmi-window-stack"></i></span>
      <span class="gm-accordion__text">
        <span class="gm-accordion__title">Web development</span>
        <span class="gm-accordion__meta">6 technologies</span>
      </span>
      <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-down gm-accordion__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    </summary>
    <div class="gm-accordion__content">
      <ul class="gm-accordion__list">
        <li>HTML</li>
        <li>CSS</li>
        <li>JavaScript</li>
        <li>TypeScript</li>
        <li>Angular</li>
        <li>.NET</li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </details>
</div>
```

## With preview and logo list

To show a list of skills or tools: closed, a few logos on the right (`.gm-accordion__preview`) and how many more there are; open, the list with a logo before each item, one below the other (`.gm-accordion__list--icons`). With `--cascade` and `style="--i: 0"`, `1`, `2`… the items come in one after the other when it opens.

```html
<div class="gm-accordion">
  <details class="gm-accordion__item" name="logos-example" open>
    <summary class="gm-accordion__summary">
      <span class="gm-accordion__icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="gmi gmi-window"></i></span>
      <span class="gm-accordion__text">
        <span class="gm-accordion__title">Frontend</span>
        <span class="gm-accordion__meta">5 technologies</span>
      </span>
      <span class="gm-accordion__preview" aria-hidden="true">
        <span class="gm-accordion__preview-item"><i class="gmi gmi-angular"></i></span>
        <span class="gm-accordion__preview-item"><i class="gmi gmi-react"></i></span>
        <span class="gm-accordion__preview-item"><i class="gmi gmi-astro"></i></span>
        <span class="gm-accordion__preview-more">+2</span>
      </span>
      <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-down gm-accordion__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    </summary>
    <ul class="gm-accordion__content gm-accordion__list gm-accordion__list--icons gm-accordion__list--cascade">
      <li style="--i: 0"><span class="gm-accordion__list-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="gmi gmi-angular"></i></span>Angular</li>
      <li style="--i: 1"><span class="gm-accordion__list-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="gmi gmi-react"></i></span>React</li>
      <li style="--i: 2"><span class="gm-accordion__list-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="gmi gmi-astro"></i></span>Astro</li>
      <li style="--i: 3"><span class="gm-accordion__list-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="gmi gmi-tailwindcss"></i></span>Tailwind CSS</li>
      <li style="--i: 4"><span class="gm-accordion__list-icon" aria-hidden="true"><i class="gmi gmi-code-slash"></i></span>WCAG (web accessibility)</li>
    </ul>
  </details>
</div>
```

On narrow screens the preview shows fewer logos (3 below 600 px) and disappears below 420 px. The logos are those in the Brand category of the [icons](/icons).

## Lists inside

If there are several items inside (more than 3), they go one below the other in a list, not run together in a sentence: `<ul class="gm-accordion__list">`. They are easier to scan and screen readers say how many there are.

## Several open at once

Without `name`, each section opens and closes on its own. With `open`, it starts open.

```html-code
<details class="gm-accordion__item" open>…</details>
```

## Accessibility

- It uses HTML `<details>` and `<summary>`: they open with the mouse, Enter or Space, and screen readers say whether they are open or closed. No JavaScript needed.
- The chevron is decorative (`aria-hidden`); the state comes from the `<details>` itself.
- The accordion border reaches 3.3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) and each row is at least 44 px tall (WCAG 2.5.5).
- The animation is removed when the person asks for reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion`).
- Do not hide information everyone needs in an accordion: use it for details only some people want.

<!-- /docs/components/alert -->
# Alert

A highlighted message inside the page: information, something that went well, a warning or an error. The state pastel at medium strength, with a border of the same color, regular text and an icon.

## Examples

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-3">
  <div class="gm-alert"><i class="gmi gmi-info-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i><span>Version 0.1 is not on npm yet.</span></div>
  <div class="gm-alert gm-alert--success" role="status"><i class="gmi gmi-check-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i><span>Changes saved.</span></div>
  <div class="gm-alert gm-alert--warning"><i class="gmi gmi-exclamation-triangle" aria-hidden="true"></i><span>You have 2 trial days left.</span></div>
  <div class="gm-alert gm-alert--danger" role="alert"><i class="gmi gmi-x-circle" aria-hidden="true"></i><span>The form could not be sent. Check your connection and try again.</span></div>
</div>
```

## Types

| Class | For | Color |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.gm-alert` | Information | Gray |
| `.gm-alert--success` | Something went well | Mint |
| `.gm-alert--warning` | Warning | Lemon |
| `.gm-alert--danger` | Error | Coral |

## Note

`.gm-alert--note`: no color or icon, on a white surface (black at night) with a soft shadow. For clarifications inside a text, like the notes in this documentation.

```html
<div class="gm-alert gm-alert--note">
  <p><strong>Tip:</strong> you can also import only the parts you use.</p>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- Color is not enough: the icon and the text also say what kind of alert it is (“Changes saved”, “Could not…”) (WCAG 1.4.1).
- If the alert appears after the person does something, add `role="status"` (calm messages) or `role="alert"` (errors): screen readers read it without moving focus (WCAG 4.1.3).
- The icon is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`).
- Text of 7:1 or more on its background in both modes (AAA).

<!-- /docs/components/ai-notice -->
# AI notice

A small note next to a chat or anything made with AI, so people know the answers come from an AI and can be wrong. With a link to more information.

## Example

```html
<p class="gm-ai-notice">
  Answers generated with AI from my profile; they may contain mistakes.
  <button type="button" class="gm-ai-notice__link" data-gm-dialog-open="example-ai-info">More about the AI</button>
</p>
<dialog class="gm-dialog" id="example-ai-info" aria-labelledby="example-ai-info-title">
  <div class="gm-dialog__body">
    <header class="gm-dialog__header">
      <h2 class="gm-dialog__title" id="example-ai-info-title">About the AI</h2>
      <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" data-gm-dialog-close aria-label="Close"><i class="gmi gmi-x-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    </header>
    <section class="gm-dialog__section"><h3>What it is</h3><p>An AI model that answers from my profile. It can be wrong: for anything important, write to me.</p></section>
  </div>
</dialog>
```

“More about the AI” opens a [dialog](/docs/components/dialog) explaining which AI it is, what happens to what people write and how to ask for it to be deleted.

## Why

- The **EU AI Act** (article 50) requires telling people they are talking to an AI.
- Data protection also asks for information about what is stored and what is not.

## Accessibility

- Gray text of 7:1 or more on the background (AAA), small but readable.
- The link sits inside the sentence, underlined, and is a button because it opens a dialog (it does not go to another page).
- Its text says what it is about (*the AI*), not just “More information”: screen readers understand it outside the sentence (WCAG 2.4.4) and search engines, which flag generic links, too.

<!-- /docs/components/avatar -->
# Avatar

The profile picture box, as a circle or a square with rounded corners. Without a photo, it shows the initials on a pastel or a silhouette.

## Shapes

Circle (`.gm-avatar`) or rounded square (`.gm-avatar--square`). The photo is cropped to fill the box without stretching.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-4">
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--lg"><img src="media/perfil-1.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--lg gm-avatar--square"><img src="media/perfil-2.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
</div>
```

## Sizes

`.gm-avatar--sm` (2 rem), default (3 rem), `.gm-avatar--lg` (5 rem) and `.gm-avatar--xl` (8 rem). The rounding and the letters grow in proportion.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-4">
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--sm"><img src="media/perfil-3.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar"><img src="media/perfil-3.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--lg"><img src="media/perfil-3.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--xl"><img src="media/perfil-3.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
</div>
```

## Without a photo

With initials: add a palette color (`.gm-theme-sky`, `.gm-theme-mint`…) and give the name with `role="img"` and `aria-label`, because initials alone are not clear. Without a name, a silhouette.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-4">
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--lg gm-theme-sky" role="img" aria-label="Sara Paez">SP</span>
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--lg gm-avatar--square gm-theme-lavender" role="img" aria-label="Sara Paez Yamuza">SP</span>
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--lg gm-theme-mint" role="img" aria-label="Diego Sanz">DS</span>
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--lg" role="img" aria-label="No profile picture"><i class="gmi gmi-person-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
</div>
```

## With a ring

`.gm-avatar--ring`: the photo with a colored ring. By default, in sky (turquoise in dark mode); the thickness is proportional to the size.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-4">
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--xl gm-avatar--ring"><img src="media/perfil-1.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--xl gm-avatar--ring gm-avatar--square"><img src="media/perfil-2.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
</div>
```

## Customize

| Variable | What it changes | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--gm-avatar-size` | The size | 3 rem |
| `--gm-avatar-radius` | How rounded the corners are | 50% (circle); 22% with `--square` |
| `--gm-avatar-ring` | The ring color (a color or a gradient), with `--ring` | Sky (turquoise in dark mode) |

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-4">
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--xl gm-avatar--ring" style="--gm-avatar-ring: var(--gm-accent)"><img src="media/perfil-3.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--xl gm-avatar--ring" style="--gm-avatar-ring: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--gm-mint), var(--gm-sky), var(--gm-lavender))"><img src="media/perfil-4.jpg" alt="Diego Sanz"></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--xl" style="--gm-avatar-radius: 0.75rem"><img src="media/perfil-1.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar" style="--gm-avatar-size: 6rem; --gm-avatar-radius: 35%"><img src="media/perfil-2.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"></span>
</div>
```

## Enlarge on click

To show the photo large when it is pressed: the box is a link to the large photo with `data-gm-zoom`, and the [gallery](/docs/components/gallery) script opens it in its viewer, without arrows or counter. A magnifier cursor shows on hover.

```html
<a class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--xl gm-avatar--ring" href="media/perfil-1.jpg" data-gm-zoom aria-label="Enlarge Sara Paez Yamuza's photo">
  <img src="media/perfil-1.jpg" alt="Sara Paez Yamuza">
</a>
```

```html-code
<script type="module">
  import { initZooms } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/gallery.js';
  initZooms();
</script>
```

The viewer closes with Escape, the ✕ or by clicking outside, and focus returns to the photo.

## Changing the photo

On the profile page, a button with the pencil on top of the photo. Use it with the large sizes (`--lg` and `--xl`): the button is 44 px.

```html
<span class="gm-avatar gm-avatar--xl">
  <img src="media/perfil-4.jpg" alt="Your profile picture">
  <button type="button" class="gm-avatar__edit" aria-label="Change profile picture"><i class="gmi gmi-pencil-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</span>
```

## Group

Several stacked photos, for example to show who is taking part. The last one can say how many more there are.

```html
<div class="gm-avatar-group" role="group" aria-label="Sara Paez Yamuza and 7 more people take part">
  <span class="gm-avatar"><img src="media/perfil-1.jpg" alt=""></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar"><img src="media/perfil-2.jpg" alt=""></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar"><img src="media/perfil-3.jpg" alt=""></span>
  <span class="gm-avatar" aria-hidden="true">+5</span>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- A photo with the name next to it (in a list of people) is decorative: `alt=""`. On its own, it carries the name: `alt="Sara Paez Yamuza"`.
- Initials go with `role="img"` and an `aria-label` with the full name.
- In a group, the group's `aria-label` says who takes part and the photos have `alt=""`.
- Initials are black on the pastel (7.8:1 or more, AAA); without a color, regular text on gray.
- The button to change the photo is 44 px (WCAG 2.5.5) and says what it does.

<!-- /docs/components/button -->
# Button

Buttons for actions in forms, dialogs and pages, with rounded shapes. All of them meet WCAG 2.2 AA in light and dark mode.

## Variants

`.gm-btn` is the main button: black in light mode and white in dark mode. Add `.gm-btn--secondary` for a glass button with a border, or `.gm-btn--ghost` for one without background.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn">Primary</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary">Secondary</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--ghost">Ghost</button>
</div>
```

## With color

Add a color of the palette (`.gm-theme-sky`, `.gm-theme-mint`…) and how to use it: `.gm-theme-solid` for the pastel with black text, or `.gm-theme-glass` for the glazed version. The button keeps its pill shape.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid">Solid</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-theme-sky gm-theme-glass">Glazed</button>
</div>
```

All the colors, solid:

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid">Sky</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-blue gm-theme-solid">Blue</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-lavender gm-theme-solid">Lavender</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-pink gm-theme-solid">Pink</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-peach gm-theme-solid">Peach</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-lemon gm-theme-solid">Lemon</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-mint gm-theme-solid">Mint</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-coral gm-theme-solid">Coral</button>
</div>
```

And glazed:

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-sky gm-theme-glass">Sky</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-blue gm-theme-glass">Blue</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-lavender gm-theme-glass">Lavender</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-pink gm-theme-glass">Pink</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-peach gm-theme-glass">Peach</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-lemon gm-theme-glass">Lemon</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-mint gm-theme-glass">Mint</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm gm-theme-coral gm-theme-glass">Coral</button>
</div>
```

The text on the pastel is always black (7.8:1 or more, AAA). Never use white text on these colors. To send a form, the accent `.gm-btn--accent` (pink by day, blue at night) of [Field](/docs/forms/field) is also available.

## Small

`.gm-btn--sm` makes it lower (38 px) and with smaller text.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm">Primary</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary gm-btn--sm">Secondary</button>
</div>
```

## With an icon

Put an icon before or after the text. It is decorative, so it has `aria-hidden="true"`.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn"><i class="gmi gmi-download" aria-hidden="true"></i>Download</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary">Next<i class="gmi gmi-arrow-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</div>
```

## Icon only

`.gm-icon-btn` is a round 42 px button. As it has no text, it needs `aria-label` with what it does.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Search"><i class="gmi gmi-search" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Settings"><i class="gmi gmi-gear" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Delete"><i class="gmi gmi-trash" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</div>
```

## Pill

`.gm-btn--pill` is a small button with the gray of the tags, for secondary actions in lists and cards. Add `.gm-btn--danger` for actions that delete. It only works on the pill, where its color reads well (9.6:1); on other buttons it changes nothing.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--pill">Edit</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--pill gm-btn--danger">Delete</button>
</div>
```

## Text

`.gm-btn-text` looks like a link but is a button, for small actions inside a text.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn-text">Show more</button>
</div>
```

## Back

`.gm-btn-back` goes back to the previous section. The arrow is decorative; if the visible text does not say where it goes, add it with a visually hidden text.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <a class="gm-btn-back" href="#"><span aria-hidden="true">‹</span> Back<span class="gm-visually-hidden">: Tools</span></a>
</div>
```

## Links that look like buttons

The classes also work on `<a>`. Use `<a>` when it goes to another page and `<button>` when it does something on the same page.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <a class="gm-btn" href="#">Read the docs</a>
  <a class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary" href="#">GitHub</a>
</div>
```

## Disabled

With the `disabled` attribute the button is paler and cannot be pressed.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-items-center gm-gap-3">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn" disabled>Primary</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary" disabled>Secondary</button>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

| Button | Contrast (light / dark) | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.gm-btn` | 16.8:1 / 15.5:1 | AAA |
| `.gm-btn--secondary`, `--ghost` | 16.6:1 / 13.9:1 | AAA |
| `.gm-btn--pill` | 13.8:1 / 12.8:1 | AAA |
| `.gm-btn--danger` | 9.6:1 / 9.8:1 | AAA |
| `.gm-btn-text` | 7:1 / 7:1 | AAA |

- The focus is always visible: a 2 px outline when you move with the keyboard.
- The area you press always measures at least 44 × 44 px (WCAG 2.5.5, AAA): in small buttons and pills an invisible layer makes it bigger without changing the look.
- A button with only an icon always needs `aria-label`.
- Disabled buttons are exempt from contrast, but explain why the action is not available when it is not obvious.

<!-- /docs/components/card -->
# Card

A glass box to group content: translucent background with blur, thin border, rounded corners and a soft shadow.

## Example

```html
<div class="gm-card gm-max-w-sm">
  <h3 class="gm-mt-0 gm-mx-0 gm-mb-2">Basic plan</h3>
  <p class="gm-muted">To get started: a one-page website with a contact form.</p>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm">See details</button>
</div>
```

## In a grid

With the [grid](/docs/layout/grid) (`.gm-grid--auto`), as many cards per row as fit.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-grid--auto gm-gap-sm" style="--gm-grid-min: 12.5rem">
  <div class="gm-card"><i class="gmi gmi-stars" aria-hidden="true" style="font-size: 1.5rem"></i><h3 class="gm-mt-2 gm-mx-0 gm-mb-1">Fast</h3><p class="gm-muted">Ready in minutes.</p></div>
  <div class="gm-card"><i class="gmi gmi-circle-half" aria-hidden="true" style="font-size: 1.5rem"></i><h3 class="gm-mt-2 gm-mx-0 gm-mb-1">Light and dark</h3><p class="gm-muted">Both modes, built in.</p></div>
  <div class="gm-card"><i class="gmi gmi-heart" aria-hidden="true" style="font-size: 1.5rem"></i><h3 class="gm-mt-2 gm-mx-0 gm-mb-1">Accessible</h3><p class="gm-muted">WCAG 2.2 AA and AAA.</p></div>
</div>
```

## The whole card as a link

If the whole card leads to another page, make the card the `<a>`. That avoids several repeated links.

With `gm-card--link`, the text keeps its normal color (not the link color) and the card rises a little on hover, like the ones in Tools.

```html
<a class="gm-card gm-card--link gm-block gm-max-w-sm" href="#">
  <strong>Palette generator</strong>
  <p class="gm-muted gm-mt-1 gm-mx-0 gm-mb-0">Create an accessible palette from one color.</p>
</a>
```

## Accessibility

- The border and shadow separate the card from the background; important content does not depend on them.
- If the card is a link, its text must say where it goes (WCAG 2.4.4).
- The last element in the card has no bottom margin, so the padding is the same top and bottom.

<!-- /docs/components/carousel -->
# Carousel

Images shown one at a time, inside a glass frame, with arrows on the sides and dots below.

## Example

Move through the slides with the arrows, the dots, by swiping or with the ← → keys.

```html
<div class="gm-carousel" data-gm-carousel aria-label="Landscapes">
  <div class="gm-carousel__track">
    <figure class="gm-carousel__slide">
      <img src="media/album-1.jpg" alt="White sun over sky blue and pink mountains">
      <figcaption class="gm-carousel__caption">Sunrise<p>First light over the mountains.</p></figcaption>
    </figure>
    <figure class="gm-carousel__slide">
      <img src="media/album-4.jpg" alt="Layered hills under a pink sky">
      <figcaption class="gm-carousel__caption">Hills<p>Three layers of hills at sunset.</p></figcaption>
    </figure>
    <figure class="gm-carousel__slide">
      <img src="media/album-7.jpg" alt="Green mountains under a lavender sky">
      <figcaption class="gm-carousel__caption">Valley<p>The valley in spring.</p></figcaption>
    </figure>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Autoplay

With `data-interval` (in milliseconds), it moves on its own and shows a pause button. It stops on hover or when using the keyboard inside, and does not autoplay if the person asks for reduced motion.

```html-code
<div class="gm-carousel" data-gm-carousel data-interval="5000" aria-label="Projects">…</div>
```

## Without text

The caption (`.gm-carousel__caption`) is optional.

```html-code
<figure class="gm-carousel__slide">
  <img src="photo.jpg" alt="Description of the photo">
</figure>
```

## Without buttons

With `.gm-carousel--peek` and no `data-gm-carousel`: photos move by swiping with a finger, the mouse or the arrow keys, and the next one peeks in from the side to show there is more. Give the track `tabindex="0"` and a name so it works with the keyboard.

```html
<div class="gm-carousel gm-carousel--peek">
  <div class="gm-carousel__track" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Landscapes (swipe to see more)">
    <figure class="gm-carousel__slide">
      <img src="media/album-2.jpg" alt="Blue sky over soft hills">
      <figcaption class="gm-carousel__caption">Sea of clouds</figcaption>
    </figure>
    <figure class="gm-carousel__slide">
      <img src="media/album-5.jpg" alt="Peach sky over mountains">
      <figcaption class="gm-carousel__caption">Sunset</figcaption>
    </figure>
    <figure class="gm-carousel__slide">
      <img src="media/album-8.jpg" alt="Pink hills at dusk">
      <figcaption class="gm-carousel__caption">Dusk</figcaption>
    </figure>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Swipe row

For quick options, like the suggested questions of a chat: everything in one row that slides sideways with a finger, the mouse or the keyboard, with no arrows or dots. The right edge fades out to show there is more. Use `.gm-scroll-row`; no script needed.

```html
<div class="gm-scroll-row gm-max-w-xs" role="group" aria-label="Quick questions">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--pill">Which technologies do you use?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--pill">How much does a website cost?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--pill">Do you build online shops?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--pill">How long does it take?</button>
</div>
```

With `.gm-scroll-row--mobile`, it only slides on phones (767 px or less); on large screens, the items wrap to the next line.

```html-code
<div class="gm-scroll-row gm-scroll-row--mobile" role="group" aria-label="Quick questions">…</div>
```

## Script

The framework provides the look. Without the script, slides move by swiping. The optional script adds the arrows, the dots and autoplay:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { initCarousels } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/carousel.js';
  initCarousels();
</script>
```

When the slide changes, it fires `gm-carousel-change` with its number (starting at 0) in `detail.index`.

## Accessibility

- The carousel is a named region (`aria-label`) and each slide says which one it is (“2 of 3”).
- Arrows and dots have names (“Next slide”, “Go to slide 2”) and are 44 px tall (WCAG 2.5.5). The active dot stands out by its longer shape, not just color.
- Slides that are not visible do not get focus (`inert`).
- With autoplay, there is a pause button and it stops with the mouse or the keyboard (WCAG 2.2.2). While autoplaying, screen readers do not announce every change.
- The caption is white with a shadow on a black gradient, so it reads over any image. Every image has its `alt`.
- Do not put the only important thing in a carousel: many people only see the first slide.
- In the swipe row, every item is reachable with Tab and the row scrolls to it on its own.

<!-- /docs/components/chat -->
# Chat

The pieces of an AI chat: the field to ask, the answer bubble and the typing dots. The chat itself (asking the AI, writing the answer letter by letter) comes from your app; the framework provides the look.

## Field to ask

A glass pill with the field and the send button. While typing, the border turns sky and a soft ring appears.

```html
<form class="gm-chat-input" role="search" aria-label="Ask me about my work">
  <label class="gm-visually-hidden" for="example-question">Write a question</label>
  <input id="example-question" class="gm-chat-input__field" autocomplete="off" placeholder="Ask me anything…">
  <button type="submit" class="gm-chat-input__send" aria-label="Send question"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-up-circle-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</form>
```

## Answer bubble

Glass with a sky border and, in dark mode, a turquoise glow. The tail points to the speaker: `.gm-bubble--tail-end` (right) or `.gm-bubble--tail-start` (left), at the height of `--gm-bubble-tail-y` (measured from the bottom on the right one; on the left one, from the top, or from the bottom with `.gm-bubble--tail-bottom`).

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-col gm-gap-6 gm-p-4">
  <div class="gm-bubble gm-bubble--tail-end gm-max-w-sm">
    <div class="gm-bubble__scroll" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Answer">
      I mostly work with Angular and .NET, and design in Figma. You can see my projects on <a href="#">GitHub</a>.
    </div>
    <button type="button" class="gm-bubble__close" aria-label="Close the answer"><i class="gmi gmi-x" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  </div>
  <div class="gm-bubble gm-bubble--tail-start gm-max-w-sm gm-ms-4">
    <div class="gm-bubble__scroll"><span class="gm-bubble__note">Picking up where we left off</span>When do you need the website?</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Thinking

While the answer arrives, `.gm-typing` with three `<span>`s: three dots bouncing, in sky (turquoise in dark mode).

```html
<div class="gm-bubble" style="max-width: 7.5rem">
  <span class="gm-typing" aria-hidden="true"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
  <span class="gm-visually-hidden">Thinking about the answer…</span>
</div>
```

## Error

`.gm-bubble--error`: the border in coral, the error color.

## Change the color

With variables, on the bubble or on any element that contains it:

| Variable | What it changes | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--gm-bubble-color` | The border and the tail of the bubble (a color or a gradient) | Sky (turquoise in dark mode) |
| `--gm-bubble-tail-color` | Only the tail, if the border is a gradient (the tail takes a color, not a gradient) | The one in `--gm-bubble-color` |
| `--gm-typing-color` | The "thinking" dots | Sky (turquoise in dark mode) |

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-col gm-gap-6 gm-p-4">
  <div class="gm-bubble gm-bubble--tail-end gm-max-w-sm" style="--gm-bubble-color: var(--gm-accent)">
    <div class="gm-bubble__scroll">With the accent color: pink by day and blue at night.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="gm-bubble gm-bubble--tail-start gm-max-w-sm gm-ms-4" style="--gm-bubble-color: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--gm-mint-700), var(--gm-sky-700)); --gm-bubble-tail-color: var(--gm-mint-700)">
    <div class="gm-bubble__scroll">With a gradient from mint to sky; the tail, in mint.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="gm-bubble" style="--gm-bubble-color: var(--gm-accent); --gm-typing-color: var(--gm-accent); max-width: 7.5rem">
    <span class="gm-typing" aria-hidden="true"><span></span><span></span><span></span></span>
    <span class="gm-visually-hidden">Thinking about the answer…</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- The field has its `<label>` (visually hidden) and the send button its name.
- If text is written letter by letter, it is decorative: announce the whole answer at once in a separate `aria-live="polite"`.
- If the answer does not fit, the text scrolls inside; with `tabindex="0"` and `role="region"` it can be moved with the keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1).
- Next to the chat, add the [AI notice](/docs/components/ai-notice): people must know they are talking to an AI.

<!-- /docs/components/chip -->
# Chip

A glass pill for quick options, like the suggested questions of a chat. It has the same glass as the accordion and, on hover, it rises a little and the border turns sky (turquoise in dark mode).

## Example

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-gap-2 gm-justify-center">
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip">Which technologies do you use?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip">How much does a website cost?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip">Do you build online shops?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip gm-chip--accent"><i class="gmi gmi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i>I want a project</button>
</div>
```

## Accent

`.gm-chip--accent` always has the colored border and semibold text: for the main action of the group.

## On phones

Many chips in a row fit better in a [swipe row](/docs/components/carousel#swipe-row), as in the template:

```html
<div class="gm-scroll-row gm-max-w-xs" role="group" aria-label="Quick questions">
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip">Which technologies do you use?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip">How much does a website cost?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip">Do you build online shops?</button>
</div>
```

## Change the borders

| Variable | What it changes | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--gm-chip-border` | The border at rest | The panel gray |
| `--gm-chip-color` | The border on hover and on the accent chip (a color or a gradient) | Sky (turquoise in dark mode) |

With the accent color at rest and on hover, and with a pastel gradient on hover:

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-gap-2 gm-justify-center">
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip" style="--gm-chip-border: var(--gm-accent); --gm-chip-color: var(--gm-accent)">What technologies do you use?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip" style="--gm-chip-color: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--gm-mint), var(--gm-sky), var(--gm-lavender))">How much does a website cost?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip gm-chip--accent" style="--gm-chip-color: var(--gm-accent)"><i class="gmi gmi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i>I want a project</button>
</div>
```

## Without a border

`.gm-chip--borderless`: only the glass, with no border at rest or on hover (it still rises a little). Use it on backgrounds where the glass stands out well.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-gap-2 gm-justify-center">
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip gm-chip--borderless">What technologies do you use?</button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-chip gm-chip--borderless">Do you build online shops?</button>
</div>
```

## Disabled

With `disabled`, or with `aria-disabled="true"` if it must stay focusable (for example, inside a swipe row while the AI is thinking).

## Accessibility

- They are `<button>` elements with text: they say what they do.
- They look smaller than 44 px, but the touch area reaches 44 px (WCAG 2.5.5).
- Text reaches 7:1 on the glass in both modes; the border, 3:1. If you change the border color, keep it at 3:1; without a border, the text is enough to tell what it is.

<!-- /docs/components/command -->
# Copy command

A glass pill with a command and its copy button, like the `npm install` on this site's home page.

## Example

```html
<div class="gm-command">
  <code class="gm-command__text">npm install glassmarshmallow</code>
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary gm-btn--sm"><i class="gmi gmi-clipboard" aria-hidden="true"></i>Copy</button>
</div>
```

Copying is up to your code (with `navigator.clipboard.writeText`). If the command does not fit, it wraps to the next line instead of spilling out.

## Accessibility

- When copying, change the button text ("Copied") and tell screen readers too with an `aria-live` region.
- The command can be selected by hand: if the clipboard is not available, it can still be copied.

<!-- /docs/components/dialog -->
# Dialog

A window that opens on top of the page to show information or ask for something, with the background dimmed behind it. It has the panel glass, sections separated by a thin line and colored headings.

## Example

```html
<button type="button" class="gm-btn" data-gm-dialog-open="example-dialog">Open the dialog</button>
<dialog class="gm-dialog" id="example-dialog" aria-labelledby="example-dialog-title">
  <div class="gm-dialog__body">
    <header class="gm-dialog__header">
      <h2 class="gm-dialog__title" id="example-dialog-title">About the AI</h2>
      <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" data-gm-dialog-close aria-label="Close"><i class="gmi gmi-x-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    </header>
    <section class="gm-dialog__section">
      <h3>What it is</h3>
      <p>The chat uses an AI model that answers from my profile and <strong>can be wrong</strong>.</p>
    </section>
    <section class="gm-dialog__section">
      <h3>What happens to what you write</h3>
      <h4>Quick questions</h4>
      <p>Your question is only used to give you the answer. It is not stored.</p>
      <h4>“I want a project”</h4>
      <ol>
        <li>The assistant asks you a few questions about your project.</li>
        <li>At the end, it shows you a summary and offers to send it to me.</li>
        <li>If you do not send it, nothing reaches me.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>
  </div>
</dialog>
```

## Parts

| Class | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.gm-dialog` | The window (an HTML `<dialog>`) |
| `.gm-dialog__body` | The content; scrolls if it does not fit |
| `.gm-dialog__header` | Title and close button |
| `.gm-dialog__title` | The title; it gets focus when opened |
| `.gm-dialog__section` | Each section, with a line above; its `<h3>`s are colored |

## Script

The optional script opens the dialog with `data-gm-dialog-open="id"` and closes it with `data-gm-dialog-close`, Escape or clicking outside:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { initDialogs, openDialog } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/dialog.js';
  initDialogs();
  // or from your code: openDialog(document.getElementById('my-dialog'));
</script>
```

## Accessibility

- It is an HTML `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()`: the rest of the page becomes inert, so neither the mouse, the keyboard nor screen readers leave the dialog while it is open.
- It is named with `aria-labelledby` (its title) and screen readers announce it as a dialog.
- When opened, focus goes to the title, not the ✕, so it is read from the start. When closed, it returns to the button that opened it.
- Escape always closes it, and the close button says what it does (“Close”).
- Use it sparingly: it interrupts. For short messages, an [alert](/docs/components/alert) on the page is better.

<!-- /docs/components/footer -->
# Footer

A footer with a heading, icon links (email and social), the legal links on one line and the name with the year. Centered, with a thin line above.

## Example

```html
<footer class="gm-footer">
  <div class="gm-container">
    <h2>Let's connect</h2>
    <div class="gm-footer__socials">
      <a href="#" aria-label="Send an email"><i class="gmi gmi-envelope-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i></a>
      <a href="#" aria-label="GitHub (opens in a new tab)"><i class="gmi gmi-github" aria-hidden="true"></i></a>
    </div>
    <nav class="gm-footer__links" aria-label="Legal information">
      <a href="#">Privacy</a><span aria-hidden="true">·</span><a href="#">Legal notice</a>
    </nav>
    <p class="gm-footer__bottom">2026 · <strong>Sara Paez Yamuza</strong> · Portfolio</p>
    <p class="gm-footer__credit">Made with <a href="#">GlassMarshmallow</a></p>
  </div>
</footer>
```

## Parts

| Class | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.gm-footer` | The footer, centered with a line above |
| `.gm-footer__socials` | 32 px icon links (email, social) |
| `.gm-footer__links` | Legal links on one line, underlined and gray |
| `.gm-footer__bottom` | The year and the name (in `<strong>`) |
| `.gm-footer__credit` | Credits, smaller |

## Large social icons

For email and social links outside the footer (for example, on the home page): `.gm-socials`, 36 px icons that grow a little on hover. Change the size with `--gm-socials-size`.

```html
<div class="gm-socials">
  <button type="button" aria-label="Copy email address"><i class="gmi gmi-envelope-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <a href="#" aria-label="GitHub (opens in a new tab)"><i class="gmi gmi-github" aria-hidden="true"></i></a>
  <a href="#" aria-label="LinkedIn (opens in a new tab)"><i class="gmi gmi-linkedin" aria-hidden="true"></i></a>
</div>
```

## Brand logos

GitHub and LinkedIn are in the GlassMarshmallow icons (`gmi-github`, `gmi-linkedin`), with their official shape: brands do not allow their logo to be redrawn. For other brands, use their official SVG or the one from [Simple Icons](https://simpleicons.org) (free license), with `fill="currentColor"` so it takes the text color.

## Simple footer

`gm-site-footer`: a row of links and the credits below, on the page background with a line on top. It is the one on this site. Over the full-page lights background (`gm-backdrop`), it turns white in light mode and black in dark mode, with no line, to continue the gradient at the end. With `gm-has-tabbar` it leaves room for the phone tab bar.

```html
<footer class="gm-site-footer">
  <div class="gm-site-footer__inner">
    <nav class="gm-site-footer__links" aria-label="Footer">
      <a href="#">Docs</a><a href="#">Examples</a><a href="#">Icons</a>
    </nav>
    <p class="gm-site-footer__credit gm-muted gm-small">Designed and built by <a class="gm-site-footer__author" href="#">Sara Paez Yamuza</a> · MIT License</p>
  </div>
</footer>
```

## Accessibility

- Icon-only links have an `aria-label` (“Send an email”, “GitHub, opens in a new tab”).
- Each link is at least 44 px (WCAG 2.5.5).
- The legal links go in a named `<nav>`.

<!-- /docs/components/gallery -->
# Photo gallery

An album: photos in a grid, all the same size, with more columns on large screens and fewer on phones. Pressing one shows it large in a viewer with arrows to move to the next.

## Example

```html
<div class="gm-gallery" data-gm-gallery aria-label="Landscapes">
  <a class="gm-gallery__item" href="media/album-1.jpg" data-caption="Sunrise"><img src="media/album-1.jpg" alt="White sun over sky blue and pink mountains"></a>
  <a class="gm-gallery__item" href="media/album-2.jpg" data-caption="Sea of clouds"><img src="media/album-2.jpg" alt="Blue sky over soft hills"></a>
  <a class="gm-gallery__item" href="media/album-3.jpg" data-caption="Summer afternoon"><img src="media/album-3.jpg" alt="Layered mountains under a lavender sky"></a>
  <a class="gm-gallery__item" href="media/album-4.jpg" data-caption="Hills"><img src="media/album-4.jpg" alt="Layered hills under a pink sky"></a>
  <a class="gm-gallery__item" href="media/album-5.jpg" data-caption="Sunset"><img src="media/album-5.jpg" alt="Peach sky over mountains"></a>
  <a class="gm-gallery__item" href="media/album-6.jpg" data-caption="Full moon"><img src="media/album-6.jpg" alt="White moon over yellow hills"></a>
</div>
```

## Square and with text

`.gm-gallery--square` crops photos to squares. For a text under each one, add `.gm-gallery__caption` inside the link.

```html
<div class="gm-gallery gm-gallery--square" data-gm-gallery aria-label="Trip">
  <a class="gm-gallery__item" href="media/album-7.jpg"><img src="media/album-7.jpg" alt="Green valley under a lavender sky"><span class="gm-gallery__caption">Valley</span></a>
  <a class="gm-gallery__item" href="media/album-8.jpg"><img src="media/album-8.jpg" alt="Pink hills at dusk"><span class="gm-gallery__caption">Dusk</span></a>
  <a class="gm-gallery__item" href="media/album-9.jpg"><img src="media/album-9.jpg" alt="Sky blue mountains at noon"><span class="gm-gallery__caption">Noon</span></a>
</div>
```

## Larger photos

`.gm-gallery--lg`: columns of at least 300 px instead of 200 px.

```html-code
<div class="gm-gallery gm-gallery--lg" data-gm-gallery aria-label="Portfolio">…</div>
```

## Script

The framework provides the look. Without the script, each photo opens the large image in the same tab. The optional script shows it in the viewer:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { initGalleries } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/gallery.js';
  initGalleries();
</script>
```

- Each photo's `href` is the large image; the thumbnail (`<img>`) can be a lighter version.
- The viewer text comes from `data-caption` or, if missing, from the thumbnail's `alt`.

## A single photo

To enlarge a single photo (for example, the [profile photo](/docs/components/avatar#enlarge-on-click)): a link to the large photo with `data-gm-zoom` and `initZooms()`. The viewer shows without arrows or counter.

## Keyboard

In the viewer:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ← → | Previous or next photo |
| Home / End | First or last photo |
| Escape | Closes the viewer and focus returns to the photo |

## Accessibility

- Each photo is a link with its `alt`, so it opens with the keyboard and screen readers say what it is.
- The viewer is a `<dialog>`: focus stays inside and Escape closes it. The counter (“2 of 9”) is announced when the photo changes.
- Arrows and close have names and are 44 px (WCAG 2.5.5); on a nearly black background, with white border and focus.
- The gentle zoom on hover is removed when the person asks for reduced motion.

<!-- /docs/components/tag -->
# Tag

A small pill to label something: a category, a status, something new.

## Example

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-gap-2">
  <span class="gm-tag">Novel</span>
  <span class="gm-tag">Fantasy</span>
  <span class="gm-tag">2026</span>
</div>
```

## With color

With the palette colors (`.gm-theme-…` and `.gm-theme-solid`), black text on the pastel.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-gap-2">
  <span class="gm-tag gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid">New</span>
  <span class="gm-tag gm-theme-mint gm-theme-solid">Read</span>
  <span class="gm-tag gm-theme-lemon gm-theme-solid">Pending</span>
  <span class="gm-tag gm-theme-coral gm-theme-solid">Sold out</span>
</div>
```

## Tag or button

A tag only informs: it is not pressed. To filter or choose, use a pill button (`.gm-btn--pill`) or the [segmented control](/docs/forms/segmented).

## Accessibility

- The tag text says what it means; color only reinforces it (WCAG 1.4.1).
- Regular text on gray (14:1) or black on pastel (7.8:1 or more): AAA.
- It does not look like a button (no border, no hover effect), to avoid confusion.

<!-- /docs/components/navbar -->
# Navbar

The top bar: logo and name on the left, the section links and, on the right, the actions (language, theme…). It is glass and sticks to the top when scrolling.

## Example

On the site it sticks to the top (`position: sticky`); here it is shown inside the frame.

```html
<header class="gm-navbar gm-relative gm-rounded-sm">
  <a class="gm-navbar__brand" href="#"><img class="gm-navbar__logo" src="logo.svg" alt="" width="48" height="48"><span>My site</span></a>
  <nav class="gm-navbar__nav" aria-label="Main">
    <a href="#" aria-current="page">Home</a>
    <a href="#">Services</a>
    <a href="#">Contact</a>
  </nav>
  <div class="gm-navbar__actions">
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Switch to dark mode"><i class="gmi gmi-moon" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  </div>
</header>
```

## Parts

| Class | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `.gm-navbar` | The bar: glass, sticky, as wide as the container |
| `.gm-navbar__brand` | Logo and name (link to home) |
| `.gm-navbar__logo` | The logo, 48 px (42 px on phones) |
| `.gm-navbar__nav` | The section links; the current page has `aria-current="page"` and is bold. On a one-page site, the section being viewed has `aria-current="location"` |
| `.gm-navbar__actions` | Buttons on the right (language, theme, account…) |

## Glass logo

If the logo is made of glass (translucent, with shiny edges, like the GlassMarshmallow one), it barely shows on a light background. Add `.gm-glass-logo`: in light mode it gets a thin white border and the medium shadow outside, and the glass stays clean, as in dark mode; in dark mode nothing changes. It also works outside the navbar, for example in a card.

```html
<img class="gm-navbar__logo gm-glass-logo" src="logo.svg" alt="" width="48" height="48">
```

## Without a logo and floating on phones

For single-page sites. **On computers**, without a logo: the links in the center and the theme button on the right (`.gm-navbar--centered`). **On phones**, no bar: only the round glass buttons remain, floating at the top right (`.gm-navbar--floating`), and the menu button (`.gm-navbar__menu`) opens the [full-screen menu](/docs/components/fullscreen-menu).

```html
<header class="gm-navbar gm-navbar--centered gm-navbar--floating gm-relative gm-rounded-sm">
  <nav class="gm-navbar__nav" aria-label="Centered bar example">
    <a href="#" aria-current="page">Home</a>
    <a href="#">About me</a>
    <a href="#">Skills</a>
  </nav>
  <div class="gm-navbar__actions">
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Switch to dark mode"><i class="gmi gmi-moon" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn gm-icon-btn--glass gm-navbar__menu" aria-label="Open menu"><i class="gmi gmi-list" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  </div>
</header>
```

This is how it looks on phones (make the window narrower than 860 px to see it in the top bar):

```html
<div class="gm-relative gm-overflow-hidden gm-rounded-sm" style="height: 10rem; background: var(--gm-backdrop-lights), var(--gm-backdrop-bg)">
  <div class="gm-absolute gm-flex gm-gap-3" style="top: 0.75rem; right: 0.75rem">
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn gm-icon-btn--glass" aria-label="Switch to dark mode"><i class="gmi gmi-moon" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn gm-icon-btn--glass" aria-label="Open menu"><i class="gmi gmi-list" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Change the colors

With variables on the bar:

| Variable | What it changes |
| --- | --- |
| `--gm-header-bg` | The background (a color, with transparency if you want glass) |
| `--gm-header-filter` | The glass blur (`blur(24px)`; `none` to remove it) |
| `--gm-header-border` | The bottom line |
| `--gm-header-shadow` | The shadow |
| `--gm-nav-size` | The link size (0.88 rem; 1 rem in the bar without a logo) |
| `--gm-nav-link` | The link color |
| `--gm-nav-link-hover` | The link color on hover (a color or a gradient). By default, the accent: the strong one by day (dark pink, 8.6:1) and the normal one at night (blue, or turquoise with `gm-accent-turquoise`) |

So the text reads well on the new background, the easiest way is to fix the mode of the bar with `data-theme`: a dark bar on a light page (`data-theme="dark"`) or a pastel with black text (`data-theme="light"`).

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-4">
  <header class="gm-navbar gm-navbar--centered gm-relative gm-rounded-sm" data-theme="dark">
    <nav class="gm-navbar__nav" aria-label="Dark bar example">
      <a href="#" aria-current="page">Home</a><a href="#">About me</a><a href="#">Skills</a>
    </nav>
    <div class="gm-navbar__actions"><button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Switch to light mode"><i class="gmi gmi-sun" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></div>
  </header>
  <header class="gm-navbar gm-navbar--centered gm-relative gm-rounded-sm" data-theme="light" style="--gm-header-bg: var(--gm-mint); --gm-header-border: transparent; --gm-header-shadow: 0 4px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, .08)">
    <nav class="gm-navbar__nav" aria-label="Mint bar example">
      <a href="#" aria-current="page">Home</a><a href="#">About me</a><a href="#">Skills</a>
    </nav>
    <div class="gm-navbar__actions"><button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Switch to dark mode"><i class="gmi gmi-moon" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></div>
  </header>
</div>
```

### On hover

Hover over the links: in the first bar they take the accent color (pink by day, blue at night); in the second, a gradient from lavender to pink.

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-gap-4">
  <header class="gm-navbar gm-navbar--centered gm-relative gm-rounded-sm" style="--gm-nav-link-hover: var(--gm-accent)">
    <nav class="gm-navbar__nav" aria-label="Accent color example">
      <a href="#" aria-current="page">Home</a><a href="#">About me</a><a href="#">Skills</a>
    </nav>
  </header>
  <header class="gm-navbar gm-navbar--centered gm-relative gm-rounded-sm" data-theme="light" style="--gm-nav-link-hover: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--gm-lavender-700), var(--gm-pink-700))">
    <nav class="gm-navbar__nav" aria-label="Gradient example">
      <a href="#" aria-current="page">Home</a><a href="#">About me</a><a href="#">Skills</a>
    </nav>
  </header>
</div>
```

To change the accent color of the whole site (also buttons, focus and fields), see [Another accent color](/docs/getting-started/css-variables#another-accent-color).

For the whole site, put the variables in `:root` (and the night ones in `[data-theme="dark"]`), as in [CSS variables](/docs/getting-started/css-variables).

## Like the one on this site

This documentation's bar combines parts that work for any site with many pages:

- `gm-navbar__start`: the brand and the links together on the left; the rest (search, actions) stays on the right.
- `gm-navbar__icon`: an icon link in the actions, like the GitHub one, with a 44 px target.
- `gm-glass-logo--backdrop`: the glass logo with the home page lights behind it in light mode, instead of the shadow.
- `gm-search--collapse-lg` (on the search): it turns into the magnifying glass up to 1100 px instead of 860 px, for bars with many or long links (like this one in Spanish), and between 1100 and 1300 px the field gets narrower if needed so it never covers a link.
- `gm-navbar--dense`: on phones, brand, logo and buttons closer together so search, language and theme fit; below 360 px, only the logo (screen readers still read the name).

```html-code
<header class="gm-navbar gm-navbar--dense">
  <div class="gm-navbar__start">
    <a class="gm-navbar__brand" href="/"><img class="gm-navbar__logo gm-glass-logo gm-glass-logo--backdrop" src="logo.svg" alt=""><span>GlassMarshmallow</span></a>
    <nav class="gm-navbar__nav" aria-label="Main">…</nav>
  </div>
  <div class="gm-search gm-search--navbar gm-search--collapse-lg" role="search">…</div>
  <div class="gm-navbar__actions">
    <a class="gm-navbar__icon" href="https://github.com/…" aria-label="GitHub"><svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg></a>
    …
  </div>
</header>
```

## On phones

Below 860 px, the `.gm-navbar__nav` links are hidden and move to the [tab bar](/docs/components/tabbar) at the bottom. Between 860 and 1024 px the name next to the logo is hidden so everything fits.

## Accessibility

- Links go in a named `<nav>` (`aria-label="Main"`) and the current page is marked with `aria-current="page"`, which also shows in bold.
- Each link is 44 px tall (WCAG 2.5.5).
- On hover or press, links take the accent color: dark pink by day and blue at night, both 7:1 or more (AAA).
- Focused items are not hidden behind the bar: the page leaves room when scrolling (WCAG 2.4.12).

<!-- /docs/components/tabbar -->
# Tab bar

The phone's bottom bar, floating and glass, like in iOS. It replaces the [navbar](/docs/components/navbar) links below 860 px.

## Example

On the site it only appears on phones and floats over the page (`position: fixed`); here it is shown inside the frame.

```html
<nav class="gm-tabbar gm-relative gm-flex gm-max-w-sm" aria-label="Main (mobile)" style="inset: auto">
  <a href="#" aria-current="page"><i class="gmi gmi-house" aria-hidden="true"></i>Home</a>
  <a href="#"><i class="gmi gmi-book" aria-hidden="true"></i>Docs</a>
  <a href="#"><i class="gmi gmi-heart" aria-hidden="true"></i>Icons</a>
  <button type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="example-more"><i class="gmi gmi-grid" aria-hidden="true"></i>More</button>
</nav>
```

## “More” panel

What does not fit in the bar goes in a panel opened with the “More” button (`.gm-tabbar-more`, with `.is-open` to show it).

```html-code
<nav id="mobile-more" class="gm-tabbar-more is-open" aria-label="More sections">
  <a href="/tools"><i class="gmi gmi-palette" aria-hidden="true"></i>Tools</a>
  <a href="/blog"><i class="gmi gmi-journal-text" aria-hidden="true"></i>Blog</a>
</nav>
```

## Rules

- **4 buttons at most, counting “More”**: with more, labels do not fit and buttons get too small.
- Each button has an icon and a short label (one word).
- The page leaves a gap at the end so the bar does not cover content: add `.gm-has-tabbar` to the `<body>` or the page container.

## Accessibility

- It is a named `<nav>`; the current page has `aria-current="page"` and shows in the text color (the rest in gray).
- “More” is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; Escape closes the panel.
- Focused items are not hidden behind the bar (WCAG 2.4.12).

<!-- /docs/components/fullscreen-menu -->
# Fullscreen menu

A mobile menu: a round glass button with the hamburger opens the links in large type, filling the whole screen over a nearly opaque background. It is another way to navigate on phones, for sites with few sections; the other is the [tab bar](/docs/components/tabbar).

## Example

```html
<button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn gm-icon-btn--glass" aria-controls="example-mobile-menu" aria-label="Open menu"><i class="gmi gmi-list" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
<div class="gm-fullscreen-menu" id="example-mobile-menu" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Menu">
  <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn gm-icon-btn--glass gm-fullscreen-menu__close" aria-label="Close menu"><i class="gmi gmi-x-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <nav aria-label="Mobile menu">
    <ul class="gm-fullscreen-menu__links">
      <li><a href="#" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
      <li><a href="#">About me</a></li>
      <li><a href="#">Skills</a></li>
      <li><a href="#">Contact</a></li>
    </ul>
  </nav>
</div>
```

## Round glass button

`.gm-icon-btn--glass` is the template's 44 px glass circle, meant to sit on an illustration or an image: the menu button, the close button and the light/dark switch.

## Script

```html
<script type="module">
  import { initFullscreenMenus } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/fullscreen-menu.js';
  initFullscreenMenus();
</script>
```

The button that opens it is linked to the menu with `aria-controls="menu-id"`.

## Accessibility

- When closed, the menu is inert: it cannot be reached with the keyboard nor read by screen readers.
- When open, the rest of the page is inert, focus goes to the first link and the button says `aria-expanded="true"`.
- It closes with Escape, the ✕ or by choosing a link, and focus returns to the menu button.
- Large links (2 rem) at least 44 px tall; the current page with `aria-current="page"`.

<!-- /docs/components/menu -->
# Menu

A button that opens a list of options, like the language, version and theme menus of the top bar. One option can be marked as chosen.

## Example

Open it with the mouse or with the keyboard (Enter or Space on the button).

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-items-start gm-justify-end" style="min-height: 14.375rem">
  <div class="gm-menu" data-gm-menu>
    <button type="button" class="gm-menu__trigger" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Theme: Auto">
      <i class="gmi gmi-circle-half" aria-hidden="true"></i>
      <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-expand gm-menu__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    </button>
    <ul class="gm-menu__list" role="menu" aria-label="Theme" hidden>
```
