```html
      <li role="none"><button type="button" class="gm-menu__item" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false" data-value="light"><i class="gmi gmi-sun" aria-hidden="true"></i><span>Light</span><i class="gmi gmi-check gm-menu__check" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></li>
      <li role="none"><button type="button" class="gm-menu__item" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false" data-value="dark"><i class="gmi gmi-moon" aria-hidden="true"></i><span>Dark</span><i class="gmi gmi-check gm-menu__check" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></li>
      <li role="none"><button type="button" class="gm-menu__item" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="true" data-value="auto"><i class="gmi gmi-circle-half" aria-hidden="true"></i><span>Auto</span><i class="gmi gmi-check gm-menu__check" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Aligned to the left

The list opens aligned to the right of the button. Next to the left edge, add `.gm-menu--start`.

```html
<div style="min-height: 11.875rem">
  <div class="gm-menu gm-menu--start" data-gm-menu>
    <button type="button" class="gm-menu__trigger" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="EN, language: English">
      <i class="gmi gmi-translate" aria-hidden="true"></i> EN
      <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-expand gm-menu__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    </button>
    <ul class="gm-menu__list" role="menu" aria-label="Language" hidden>
      <li role="none"><button type="button" class="gm-menu__item" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="true" data-value="en"><span>English</span><i class="gmi gmi-check gm-menu__check" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></li>
      <li role="none"><button type="button" class="gm-menu__item" role="menuitemradio" aria-checked="false" data-value="es"><span>Español</span><i class="gmi gmi-check gm-menu__check" aria-hidden="true"></i></button></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Centered, with a regular button

`.gm-menu--center` centers the list under the button. The button can be any [button](/docs/components/button) (`.gm-btn`): it keeps its size and, with `gm-theme-solid`, its theme color. Like "For agents" on this site's home page.

```html
<div style="min-height: 12.5rem; text-align: center">
  <div class="gm-menu gm-menu--center" data-gm-menu>
    <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-theme-pink-blue gm-theme-solid gm-menu__trigger" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">
      <i class="gmi gmi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i>For agents
      <i class="gmi gmi-chevron-expand gm-menu__chevron" aria-hidden="true"></i>
    </button>
    <ul class="gm-menu__list" role="menu" aria-label="For agents" hidden>
      <li role="none"><a class="gm-menu__item" role="menuitem" href="#"><span>AI docs</span></a></li>
      <li role="none"><a class="gm-menu__item" role="menuitem" href="#"><span>All the skills</span></a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Script

The framework gives the look. To open, close and move with the keyboard, load the optional script:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { initMenus } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/menu.js';
  initMenus();
</script>
```

When an option is chosen, the menu sends the `gm-menu-select` event with the `data-value` of the option:

```js
document.querySelector('.gm-menu').addEventListener('gm-menu-select', (event) => {
  console.log(event.detail.value); // 'dark'
});
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter / Space | Opens the menu (on the button) or chooses the option |
| ↓ ↑ | Next or previous option |
| Home / End | First or last option |
| Tab | Goes around the options without leaving the menu |
| Escape | Closes the menu and goes back to the button |

## Accessibility

- The button has `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and an `aria-label` that says what is chosen («Theme: Auto»).
- The options are `menuitemradio` with `aria-checked`; the check icon is only visual.
- Button and options measure 44 px (WCAG 2.5.5, AAA). Text 15:1 or more.

<!-- /docs/components/search -->
# Search

A text field with the magnifier inside and, below it, the results that match what is typed. It is the search box in the top bar of this site.

## Example

Type, for example, “color” or “button”.

```html
<div style="min-height: 18.75rem">
  <div class="gm-search gm-max-w-xs" role="search" data-gm-search data-results-text="{count} results">
    <div class="gm-search__field">
      <i class="gmi gmi-search" aria-hidden="true"></i>
      <label class="gm-visually-hidden" for="example-search">Search the docs</label>
      <input id="example-search" class="gm-search__input" type="search" role="combobox" autocomplete="off" aria-autocomplete="list" aria-controls="example-search-list" aria-expanded="false" placeholder="Search…" />
    </div>
    <ul id="example-search-list" class="gm-search__results" role="listbox" aria-label="Results" hidden>
      <li class="gm-search__option" role="option" data-value="button"><span class="gm-search__title">Button</span><span class="gm-search__section">Components</span></li>
      <li class="gm-search__option" role="option" data-value="menu"><span class="gm-search__title">Menu</span><span class="gm-search__section">Components</span></li>
      <li class="gm-search__option" role="option" data-value="colors"><span class="gm-search__title">Palette</span><span class="gm-search__section">Color</span></li>
      <li class="gm-search__option" role="option" data-value="text"><span class="gm-search__title">Text color</span><span class="gm-search__section">Color</span></li>
      <li class="gm-search__option" role="option" data-value="field"><span class="gm-search__title">Field</span><span class="gm-search__section">Forms</span></li>
      <li class="gm-search__option" role="option" data-value="date-picker"><span class="gm-search__title">Date picker</span><span class="gm-search__section">Forms</span></li>
      <li class="gm-search__empty" role="presentation" hidden>No results.</li>
    </ul>
    <p class="gm-visually-hidden" aria-live="polite" data-gm-search-status></p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Width

The search box takes the full width of its container. To limit it, give `.gm-search` a width (in the example, `max-width: 320px`). The results list is as wide as the field, with a minimum of 320 px; on screens of 600 px or less, exactly as wide as the field.

## Script

The framework provides the look. To filter while typing and move with the keyboard, load the optional script:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { initSearches } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/search.js';
  initSearches();
</script>
```

- Each result is an `<li role="option">`. The search looks at its text and, if present, `data-keywords` (ignoring case and accents).
- With `data-href`, choosing it goes to that address. Without it, only the event fires.
- If there is a `.gm-search__empty` inside the list, it shows when there are no results.
- The element with `data-gm-search-status` announces how many results there are; the text goes in `data-results-text`, with `{count}`.

When a result is chosen, the search box fires the `gm-search-select` event with its `data-value` and `data-href`. If you cancel it with `preventDefault()`, the page does not change (useful in apps with their own router):

```js
document.querySelector('.gm-search').addEventListener('gm-search-select', (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  router.navigate(event.detail.href);
});
```

## Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| ↓ ↑ | Next or previous result |
| Enter | Opens the highlighted result (or the first one) |
| Escape | Closes the list; if already closed, clears the text |

## Accessibility

- It follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern: the field has `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`, and the list is a `listbox` with its `option`s.
- The field has its `<label>` (hidden from view, not from screen readers) and `role="search"` marks the area as a search.
- The number of results is announced with `aria-live`.
- Field and results are 44 px tall (WCAG 2.5.5, AAA). The highlighted result has a background and a border, not just color.

<!-- /docs/components/hero -->
# Hero

The home page block: the logo, the name, one sentence and the buttons, centered. Like this site's home page.

## Example

```html
<section class="gm-container gm-hero">
  <img class="gm-hero__logo" src="/logo.svg" alt="" width="120" height="120">
  <h1>GlassMarshmallow</h1>
  <p class="gm-hero__lead">A CSS framework with glass surfaces, light and dark mode and accessibility from the first component.</p>
  <div class="gm-hero__actions">
    <a class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary" href="#">Examples</a>
    <a class="gm-btn" href="#">Read the docs</a>
  </div>
</section>
```

- The name shrinks with the screen so it fits on one line on a phone.
- `gm-hero__buttons` groups buttons that, on a phone, go one under the other with the same width (the longest one's). On a computer they stay in the row.

## Accessibility

- Only one `h1` per page: the hero one.
- The logo next to the name is decorative: `alt=""`.

<!-- /docs/components/icon-grid -->
# Icon grid

Boxes with an icon and its name, like Bootstrap Icons. It is the grid on this site's [Icons](/icons) page. As many as fit go in each row.

## Example

```html
<ul class="gm-icon-grid">
  <li><a class="gm-icon-tile" href="#"><span class="gm-icon-tile__box"><i class="gmi gmi-heart" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span class="gm-icon-tile__name">heart</span></a></li>
  <li><a class="gm-icon-tile" href="#"><span class="gm-icon-tile__box"><i class="gmi gmi-star" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span class="gm-icon-tile__name">star</span></a></li>
  <li><a class="gm-icon-tile" href="#"><span class="gm-icon-tile__box"><i class="gmi gmi-book" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span class="gm-icon-tile__name">book</span></a></li>
  <li><a class="gm-icon-tile" href="#"><span class="gm-icon-tile__box"><i class="gmi gmi-github" aria-hidden="true"></i></span><span class="gm-icon-tile__name">github</span></a></li>
</ul>
```

Long names break onto the next line instead of spilling out.

## Accessibility

- The icon is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`): the link is named by the text under it.

<!-- /docs/components/showcase -->
# Showcase

A project made with the framework: its screenshots (computer and phone, in light and dark mode) and its text. Like this site's [Examples](/examples) page.

## Example

```html
<article class="gm-card gm-showcase">
  <ul class="gm-showcase__shots">
    <li><a class="gm-showcase__shot" href="/media/examples/portfolio-escritorio-claro.jpg"><img src="/media/examples/portfolio-escritorio-claro.jpg" width="1600" height="1000" alt="Portfolio on a computer"></a><span class="gm-showcase__mode">Light</span></li>
    <li><a class="gm-showcase__shot" href="/media/examples/portfolio-escritorio-oscuro.jpg"><img src="/media/examples/portfolio-escritorio-oscuro.jpg" width="1600" height="1000" alt="Portfolio on a computer"></a><span class="gm-showcase__mode">Dark</span></li>
  </ul>
  <div class="gm-showcase__text">
    <h2>Portfolio</h2>
    <p>Sara Paez Yamuza's portfolio, made with GlassMarshmallow.</p>
    <h3>Pieces</h3>
    <ul class="gm-showcase__links">
      <li><a href="/docs/components/navbar">Navbar</a></li>
      <li><a href="/docs/components/card">Card</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</article>
```

- The screenshots go above and the text below; from 1100 px, side by side.
- For the phone screenshots (narrower), add `gm-showcase__figure--mobile` to their `li`.

## Accessibility

- Each screenshot has an `alt` that says what it shows; the mode (light or dark) goes as text under it.

<!-- /docs/components/player -->
# Video player

A video player: controls appear over the video on a black gradient, the buttons are round glass and the play button is white. While the video plays, the controls hide on their own.

## Example

Press play, try the subtitles (CC) and full screen.

```html
<div class="gm-player" data-gm-player data-title="Sample video" data-subtitle="GlassMarshmallow · 12 s">
  <video src="media/ejemplo.webm" controls playsinline preload="metadata">
    <track kind="subtitles" src="media/ejemplo-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
    <track kind="subtitles" src="media/ejemplo-es.vtt" srclang="es" label="Español">
  </video>
</div>
```

## Without a title

Without `data-title`, only the video and the controls show.

```html-code
<div class="gm-player" data-gm-player>
  <video src="movie.mp4" controls playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
</div>
```

## Size

The player takes the full width of its container with a 16:9 ratio. For another format, change `aspect-ratio`:

```html-code
<div class="gm-player" data-gm-player style="aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; max-width: 640px">…</div>
```

## Script

The framework provides the look. The optional script removes the browser controls and adds the framework ones. Without the script, the video keeps the browser controls (that is why the `<video>` has `controls`).

```html
<script type="module">
  import { initPlayers } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/player.js';
  initPlayers();
</script>
```

- Buttons: play and pause, 10 seconds back and forward, sound with its volume, the time, subtitles and full screen.
- Subtitles come from the video's `<track kind="subtitles">` (or `captions`) elements, in WebVTT format. If there are none, the button does not show.
- `data-title` and `data-subtitle` put the title on top, like the movie name and the episode.
- Texts are in Spanish if the page has `<html lang="es">`, and in English otherwise. Change them with `initPlayers(document, { texts: { play: 'Watch' } })`.

## Keyboard

With focus inside the player:

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Space / K | Play or pause |
| ← → | 10 seconds back or forward |
| ↑ ↓ | Volume up or down |
| M | Mute or unmute |
| C | Turn subtitles on or off |
| F | Full screen |

With the mouse too: a click on the video plays or pauses, and a double click goes full screen.

## Accessibility

- Every button has a name (“Play”, “Back 10 seconds”…) and is 44 px, also on phones (WCAG 2.5.5, AAA).
- The timeline is a slider with its name and says the time in words (“1:15 of 3:20”).
- Controls come back with the mouse, on touch or with the keyboard, and do not hide while paused.
- Add subtitles to videos with speech (WCAG 1.2.2) and do not autoplay them with sound (WCAG 1.4.2): the script does not.
- Always dark, with the controls on a black gradient, so they read over any image.

<!-- /docs/components/progress -->
# Progress

How much of something is done: reading a book, uploading a file, the steps of a form. A thin line on gray with the done part in the accent color and a text below.

## Example

```html
<div class="gm-progress gm-max-w-sm">
  <progress class="gm-progress__bar" id="example-read" max="100" value="45">45 %</progress>
  <label class="gm-progress__label" for="example-read">45 % read · page 162 of 360</label>
</div>
```

## Large

`.gm-progress--lg`, when the bar is the main thing (an upload, an installation).

```html
<div class="gm-progress gm-progress--lg gm-max-w-md">
  <progress class="gm-progress__bar" id="example-upload" max="100" value="72">72 %</progress>
  <label class="gm-progress__label" for="example-upload">Uploading “novel.epub”: 72 %</label>
</div>
```

## Unknown duration

Without `value`, the bar shows a segment moving back and forth: work is happening, but how much is left is unknown.

```html
<div class="gm-progress gm-max-w-sm">
  <progress class="gm-progress__bar" id="example-loading" max="100">Loading</progress>
  <label class="gm-progress__label" for="example-loading">Loading the library…</label>
</div>
```

## Changing the value

It is an HTML `<progress>`: change it with its `value`.

```js
document.querySelector('#read').value = 60;
```

## Accessibility

- Use `<progress>` with its `max` and `value`: screen readers say the percentage. The `<label>` gives it a name.
- Also write the data in the text (“45 % read”): the bar alone does not give the exact number.
- The done part reaches more than 3:1 on the gray in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11), and the gray text 7:1 (AAA).
- If progress changes on its own (an upload), announce the end with a status message (`role="status"`), not every change.
- No motion if the person asks for it (`prefers-reduced-motion`).

<!-- /docs/components/sidenav -->
# Side navigation

The menu of sections next to the content, like the one in this documentation. On desktop it stays in view while scrolling; below 860 px (`md`) it hides behind a button.

## Example

```html
<nav class="gm-sidenav is-open gm-static gm-max-w-xs" aria-label="Documentation">
  <div class="gm-sidenav__group">
    <h2 class="gm-sidenav__title"><i class="gmi gmi-book" aria-hidden="true"></i>Getting started</h2>
    <ul class="gm-sidenav__list">
      <li><a class="gm-sidenav__link" href="#" aria-current="page">Introduction</a></li>
      <li><a class="gm-sidenav__link" href="#">Install</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="gm-sidenav__group">
    <h2 class="gm-sidenav__title"><i class="gmi gmi-palette" aria-hidden="true"></i>Color</h2>
    <ul class="gm-sidenav__list">
      <li><a class="gm-sidenav__link" href="#">Palette</a></li>
      <li><a class="gm-sidenav__link" href="#">Light and dark mode</a></li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</nav>
```

In the example it has `gm-static` so it stays in place and `is-open` so it also shows on phones; on a page it goes inside `gm-sidenav-layout`.

## With the content next to it

`gm-sidenav-layout` puts the menu on the left (13.75 rem) and the content on the right. On narrow screens the menu moves to the top, hidden, and the `gm-sidenav__toggle` button opens it: your code adds `.is-open` to the menu and `aria-expanded="true"` to the button.

```html-code
<div class="gm-sidenav-layout gm-container">
  <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary gm-btn--sm gm-sidenav__toggle" aria-controls="docs-menu" aria-expanded="false">
    <i class="gmi gmi-list" aria-hidden="true"></i>Browse docs
  </button>
  <nav id="docs-menu" class="gm-sidenav" aria-label="Documentation">…</nav>
  <main class="gm-sidenav-layout__main">…</main>
</div>
```

| Class | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `gm-sidenav-layout` | The grid: menu and content |
| `gm-sidenav-layout__main` | The content (it can shrink without overflowing) |
| `gm-sidenav__toggle` | The button that opens the menu on phones (hidden on desktop) |
| `gm-sidenav` | The menu: white panel in light mode and black in dark mode, fixed while scrolling |
| `gm-sidenav__group` / `__title` / `__list` / `__link` | Each section, its title with an icon, its list and its links |

## Accessibility

- It is a `<nav>` with an `aria-label`, and each section has a heading and a list: screen readers can go through it in parts.
- The current page has `aria-current="page"`: it is announced and shown in the text color and semibold, not by color alone.
- Links are 44 px tall (WCAG 2.5.5) and the gray reaches 7:1 (AAA).
- On phones, the button says with `aria-expanded` whether the menu is open and with `aria-controls` what it opens.

<!-- /docs/components/toc -->
# Table of contents

"On this page": the sections of a long page, to jump to each one. On wide screens it sits in a column on the right and stays in view while scrolling; below 1200 px it becomes a dropdown above the text.

## Example

```html
<aside class="gm-toc gm-static gm-block" aria-label="On this page">
  <p class="gm-toc__title">On this page</p>
  <ul class="gm-toc__list">
    <li><a class="gm-toc__link" href="#">Example</a></li>
    <li class="gm-toc__sub"><a class="gm-toc__link" href="#">With tabs</a></li>
    <li><a class="gm-toc__link" href="#">Accessibility</a></li>
  </ul>
</aside>
```

`gm-toc__sub` indents a subsection. In the example it has `gm-static` so it stays in place and `gm-block` so it also shows on narrow screens.

## Dropdown (phones)

`gm-toc--collapsible` on a `<details>`: it opens and closes with no code.

```html
<details class="gm-toc gm-toc--collapsible gm-block">
  <summary>On this page</summary>
  <ul class="gm-toc__list">
    <li><a class="gm-toc__link" href="#">Example</a></li>
    <li><a class="gm-toc__link" href="#">Accessibility</a></li>
  </ul>
</details>
```

In the example it has `gm-block` so it also shows on wide screens.

## With the text next to it

`gm-toc-layout` puts the text on the left and the table of contents on the right (12.5 rem). It holds both: the column and the dropdown, and each one shows at its screen size.

```html-code
<div class="gm-toc-layout">
  <article>
    <details class="gm-toc gm-toc--collapsible">…</details>
    …the text…
  </article>
  <aside class="gm-toc" aria-label="On this page">…</aside>
</div>
```

## Accessibility

- The column is an `<aside>` with an `aria-label`; the dropdown, a `<details>` the browser already makes accessible.
- Links are 44 px tall (WCAG 2.5.5).
- Each section of the text needs an `id` that matches its link.

<!-- /docs/components/pager -->
# Previous and next

Two glass cards at the end of a page that belongs to a series (documentation, a course, a step-by-step tutorial), with the name of the previous and the next page.

## Example

```html
<nav class="gm-pager" aria-label="More pages">
  <a class="gm-pager__link" href="#">
    <span class="gm-pager__label"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-left" aria-hidden="true"></i>Previous</span>
    <span class="gm-pager__title">Button</span>
  </a>
  <a class="gm-pager__link gm-pager__link--next" href="#">
    <span class="gm-pager__label">Next<i class="gmi gmi-arrow-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></span>
    <span class="gm-pager__title">Card</span>
  </a>
</nav>
```

`gm-pager__link--next` always goes in the right column, even when there is no previous page (on the first page).

## Accessibility

- It is a `<nav>` with its own `aria-label`, different from the main navigation's.
- Each link says where it goes (the page name), not just "Next".
- The arrows are decorative (`aria-hidden`): the word already says it.

<!-- /docs/components/snippet -->
# Code snippet

A piece of code to copy, with its result above it when needed: the one in this documentation. A glass panel, a bar with the language (or tabs) and the copy button.

## Example

```html
<div class="gm-snippet">
  <div class="gm-snippet__example">
    <button type="button" class="gm-btn">Button</button>
  </div>
  <div class="gm-snippet__bar">
    <span class="gm-snippet__lang">html</span>
    <button type="button" class="gm-snippet__copy"><i class="gmi gmi-clipboard" aria-hidden="true"></i><span>Copy</span></button>
  </div>
  <pre class="gm-snippet__code" tabindex="0"><code>&lt;button type="button" class="gm-btn"&gt;Button&lt;/button&gt;</code></pre>
</div>
```

Without `gm-snippet__example`, it is just the code with its bar.

## With tabs

For the same example in several languages or package managers: `gm-snippet__tabs` with a `gm-snippet__tab` per option and a `<pre>` per tab (the hidden ones with `hidden`). Switching tabs and copying is up to your code.

```html
<div class="gm-snippet">
  <div class="gm-snippet__bar">
    <div class="gm-snippet__tabs" role="tablist">
      <button type="button" class="gm-snippet__tab" role="tab" aria-selected="true">npm</button>
      <button type="button" class="gm-snippet__tab" role="tab" aria-selected="false">pnpm</button>
    </div>
    <button type="button" class="gm-snippet__copy"><i class="gmi gmi-clipboard" aria-hidden="true"></i><span>Copy</span></button>
  </div>
  <pre class="gm-snippet__code" tabindex="0" role="tabpanel"><code>npm install glassmarshmallow</code></pre>
</div>
```

| Class | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `gm-snippet` | The glass panel |
| `gm-snippet__example` | The result, on white (black at night) to see the colors as they are |
| `gm-snippet__bar` | The bar: language or tabs on the left and copy on the right |
| `gm-snippet__lang` | The language name, in small caps |
| `gm-snippet__tabs` / `gm-snippet__tab` | The tabs, like a segmented control |
| `gm-snippet__copy` | The copy button |
| `gm-snippet__code` | The `<pre>` with the code (it scrolls sideways if it does not fit) |

## Accessibility

- The code can be reached with the keyboard (`tabindex="0"` on the `<pre>`) and scrolled sideways when long.
- The tabs and the copy button are 44 × 44 px where you press them, even if they look smaller (WCAG 2.5.5).
- When copying, tell screen readers ("Code copied") with an `aria-live` region.
- Tabs have `role="tab"` and `aria-selected`; each code block, `role="tabpanel"`.

<!-- /docs/components/ticker -->
# Logo ticker

A strip that slowly moves from right to left with logos and names, for example the technologies of a project. Dark glass (white by day) with a thin border above and below, sky by day and turquoise at night.

## Example

The content goes **twice in a row** inside `.gm-ticker__track`, so the loop is seamless.

```html
<div class="gm-ticker">
  <div class="gm-ticker__track" aria-hidden="true">
    <span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-angular"></i>Angular</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-typescript"></i>TypeScript</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-database"></i>PostgreSQL</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-dotnet"></i></span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-figma"></i>Figma</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-ollama"></i>Ollama</span>
    <span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-angular"></i>Angular</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-typescript"></i>TypeScript</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-database"></i>PostgreSQL</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-dotnet"></i></span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-figma"></i>Figma</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-ollama"></i>Ollama</span>
  </div>
  <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn gm-icon-btn--glass gm-ticker__pause" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Pause the strip"><i class="gmi gmi-pause-fill" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</div>
```

## Static

`.gm-ticker--static`: no movement, with the logos that fit centered (for example, when the page has no animations). Then one copy is enough.

```html
<div class="gm-ticker gm-ticker--static" aria-hidden="true">
  <div class="gm-ticker__track"><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-angular"></i>Angular</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-typescript"></i>TypeScript</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-database"></i>PostgreSQL</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-dotnet"></i></span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-figma"></i>Figma</span><span class="gm-ticker__item"><i class="gmi gmi-ollama"></i>Ollama</span></div>
</div>
```

## Pausing it

The round button with the pause icon (`.gm-ticker__pause`) goes at the end of the strip, without taking up space. With the optional script, pressing it stops the strip (`.is-paused`), the icon changes to play and the button says it is pressed (its name, “Pause the strip”, does not change):

```html-code
<script type="module">
  import { initTickers } from 'glassmarshmallow/js/ticker.js';
  initTickers();
</script>
```

It also stops on its own on hover or with focus inside, and it does not move if the person asks for reduced motion.

## Accessibility

- The logos are **decorative** (`aria-hidden="true"` on `.gm-ticker__track`): the same information must be elsewhere on the page (in the template, the Skills section).
- It moves on its own for more than 5 seconds, so it has the button to stop it, reachable with the keyboard and by touch (WCAG 2.2.2). When static (`--static`) it is not needed.
- It does not move if the person asks for reduced motion (WCAG 2.3.3).

<!-- /docs/components/tool -->
# Tool

The layout of this site's generators: a preview and, next to it, the controls that change it and the code to copy. Below 860 px (`md`), the preview goes on top and the controls below.

## Example

```html
<div class="gm-tool">
  <div class="gm-tool__preview">
    <div class="gm-flex gm-items-center gm-justify-center gm-rounded-md gm-border gm-p-8 gm-theme-lavender gm-theme-solid">
      <p class="gm-m-0 gm-font-bold gm-text-xl">Preview</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="gm-card gm-tool__controls">
    <div class="gm-slider">
      <label for="tool-size">Size</label>
      <output for="tool-size">24 px</output>
      <input id="tool-size" class="gm-range" type="range" min="8" max="64" value="24">
    </div>
    <fieldset class="gm-tool__group">
      <legend>Shape</legend>
      <div class="gm-flex gm-gap-2">
        <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--sm">Round</button>
        <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary gm-btn--sm">Square</button>
      </div>
    </fieldset>
    <div class="gm-tool__code">
      <pre class="gm-code gm-code--wrap"><code>font-size: 1.5rem;</code></pre>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Class | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `gm-tool` | The two columns: preview (a bit wider) and controls |
| `gm-tool__preview` | The preview column (with whatever goes below it, like a button) |
| `gm-tool__preview--sticky` | The preview stays in view while scrolling through the controls (on desktop) |
| `gm-tool__controls` | The controls, spaced out; with `gm-card`, in a card |
| `gm-tool__group` | A `<fieldset>` with no border or padding, with its `<legend>` as a heading |
| `gm-tool__code` | The generated code and its buttons |
| `gm-tool__stage` | The preview box: centered content, rounded corners, lower on a phone |
| `gm-tool__sample` | Sample text on top of the preview, with `gm-tool__sample-title` and `gm-tool__sample-small` |
| `gm-tool__toggle` | A checkbox with its text ("Show the sample text") |
| `gm-tool__presets` / `gm-tool__preset` / `gm-tool__swatch` | Buttons with starting values, each with a color sample |
| `gm-tool__stops` / `gm-tool__stop` / `gm-tool__stop-position` | A list of colors: each row with its picker, its position and the remove button |
| `gm-tool__pad` / `gm-tool__pad-btn` / `gm-tool__pad-dot` | A 3 × 3 grid of buttons for a direction or a position (with `aria-pressed`) |
| `gm-tool__fullscreen` / `gm-tool__fullscreen-bar` | A `<dialog>` that shows the result full screen, with a bar to close it |

Controls are usually [sliders with their value](/docs/forms/range) (`gm-slider`) and the code, a [code block](/docs/content/code) with `gm-code--wrap`.

## Preview with sample text

```html
<div class="gm-tool__preview">
  <div class="gm-tool__stage gm-theme-sky gm-theme-solid">
    <div class="gm-tool__sample">
      <p class="gm-tool__sample-title">Sample title</p>
      <p>This is how the text looks.</p>
      <p class="gm-tool__sample-small">Small text</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <label class="gm-tool__toggle gm-justify-self-start"><input type="checkbox" checked> Show the sample text</label>
</div>
```

## Direction pad

```html
<div class="gm-tool__pad">
  <button type="button" class="gm-tool__pad-btn" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Up left"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-up-left" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-tool__pad-btn" aria-pressed="true" aria-label="Up"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-up" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-tool__pad-btn" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Up right"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-up-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-tool__pad-btn" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Left"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-left" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <span class="gm-tool__pad-center" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <button type="button" class="gm-tool__pad-btn" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Right"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-tool__pad-btn" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Down left"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-down-left" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-tool__pad-btn" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Down"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-down" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
  <button type="button" class="gm-tool__pad-btn" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Down right"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-down-right" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
</div>
```

For positions, put a `<span class="gm-tool__pad-dot" aria-hidden="true"></span>` in each button instead of the arrow.

## Accessibility

- Every control has its name (`<label>` or `<legend>`) and its value in view (`<output>`).
- If the preview is only a picture, give it `aria-hidden="true"` and explain what changes in text.
- The HTML order is the screen order: first the preview, then the controls.

<!-- /docs/components/tooltip -->
# Tooltip

A small bubble with extra information about a button or a control. Dark background, white text and a soft shadow, in light and dark mode.

## How it works

Wrap the element and its bubble in `.gm-tooltip`. The bubble has `role="tooltip"` and an `id`, and the element points to it with `aria-describedby`, so screen readers read it.

It shows when you hover the element and when you reach it with the keyboard. Move the pointer onto the bubble and it stays open.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-justify-center gm-items-center gm-gap-3 gm-pt-12">
  <span class="gm-tooltip">
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Search" aria-describedby="tip-1"><i class="gmi gmi-search" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    <span class="gm-tooltip__bubble" role="tooltip" id="tip-1">Search the library</span>
  </span>
  <span class="gm-tooltip">
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Download" aria-describedby="tip-2"><i class="gmi gmi-download" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    <span class="gm-tooltip__bubble" role="tooltip" id="tip-2">Download the book</span>
  </span>
  <span class="gm-tooltip">
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Settings" aria-describedby="tip-3"><i class="gmi gmi-gear" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    <span class="gm-tooltip__bubble" role="tooltip" id="tip-3">Settings</span>
  </span>
</div>
```

## Below

By default it goes above. Add `.gm-tooltip--bottom` to put it below.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-justify-center gm-items-center gm-gap-3 gm-pb-12">
  <span class="gm-tooltip gm-tooltip--bottom">
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Share" aria-describedby="tip-4"><i class="gmi gmi-share" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    <span class="gm-tooltip__bubble" role="tooltip" id="tip-4">Share with a friend</span>
  </span>
</div>
```

## Next to an edge

Centered bubbles can go past the edge of the screen. Next to the left edge, add `.gm-tooltip--start`; next to the right one, `.gm-tooltip--end`.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-justify-between gm-items-center gm-gap-3 gm-pt-12">
  <span class="gm-tooltip gm-tooltip--start">
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Back" aria-describedby="tip-6"><i class="gmi gmi-arrow-left" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    <span class="gm-tooltip__bubble" role="tooltip" id="tip-6">Back to the library</span>
  </span>
  <span class="gm-tooltip gm-tooltip--end">
    <button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn" aria-label="Settings" aria-describedby="tip-7"><i class="gmi gmi-gear" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
    <span class="gm-tooltip__bubble" role="tooltip" id="tip-7">Reader settings</span>
  </span>
</div>
```

## On a button with text

A tooltip adds information; it does not replace the name of the button. On a button with text, use it to explain something more.

```html
<div class="gm-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-justify-center gm-items-center gm-gap-3 gm-pt-12">
  <span class="gm-tooltip">
    <button type="button" class="gm-btn gm-btn--secondary gm-btn--sm" aria-describedby="tip-5">Publish</button>
    <span class="gm-tooltip__bubble" role="tooltip" id="tip-5">Everyone with the link will see it</span>
  </span>
</div>
```

## Close it with Escape

WCAG 2.2 asks that a tooltip can be closed without moving the pointer or the focus. As the framework is only CSS, add this small script to your page so that the Escape key closes it:

```js
// Escape hides the open tooltip until the pointer or the focus leaves it
document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (event.key !== 'Escape') return;
  document.querySelectorAll('.gm-tooltip:hover, .gm-tooltip:focus-within')
    .forEach((tip) => tip.classList.add('is-dismissed'));
});
for (const type of ['mouseout', 'focusout']) {
  document.addEventListener(type, (event) => {
    const tip = event.target.closest?.('.gm-tooltip');
    if (tip && !tip.contains(event.relatedTarget)) tip.classList.remove('is-dismissed');
  });
}
```

## Accessibility

- White text on #1d1d1f: 16.8:1 (AAA), in light and dark mode.
- It shows with the pointer and with the keyboard, it stays open while the pointer is on it, and it closes with Escape (with the script).
- Don’t put links or buttons inside: a tooltip is only text. For interactive content, use a menu or a dialog.
- On touch screens there is no hover, so don’t put essential information only in a tooltip.
- With «reduce motion», it appears without animation.

<!-- /docs/helpers/visually-hidden -->
# Visually hidden

`.gm-visually-hidden` hides text visually but keeps it for screen readers. Use it to give context that the design shows but cannot be read.

## Example

An icon-only button: sighted people see the cross; screen reader users hear “Delete photo”.

```html
<button type="button" class="gm-icon-btn">
  <i class="gmi gmi-x-lg" aria-hidden="true"></i>
  <span class="gm-visually-hidden">Delete photo</span>
</button>
```

## When to use it

- Field labels that the design makes clear (a search box with the magnifier).
- Section headings that are not shown but help moving around with a screen reader.
- Announced messages (`aria-live`) that take no space.

## When not to

- To hide something from everyone: use `hidden` or `display: none`.
- To hide something only from screen readers (a decorative icon): use `aria-hidden="true"`.
- If the text would help everyone, better to show it.

<!-- /docs/helpers/hit-area -->
# Hit area

`gm-hit-area` enlarges the area you can press up to 44 × 44 px without changing how it looks: for icon links or buttons that look smaller. It is what the framework buttons already do inside.

## Example

```html
<a class="gm-hit-area gm-inline-flex gm-p-1" href="#" aria-label="GitHub"><i class="gmi gmi-github" aria-hidden="true"></i></a>
```

It looks the size of the icon, but responds to touch in a 44 px square around it.

## How it works

An invisible layer (`::after`) sticks out of the element as much as needed to reach 44 px wide and tall, centered. If the element is already bigger, the layer does not enlarge it.

## Accessibility

- WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA) asks for 44 × 44 px for anything pressed; WCAG 2.5.8 (AA), 24 × 24 px at least.
- Leave space between two nearby hit areas: if they overlap, a finger may press the wrong one.

<!-- /docs/helpers/skip-link -->
# Skip link

A link at the start of the page that goes straight to the content, skipping the menu. It is hidden until reached with the Tab key.

## Example

Press Tab when opening any page on this site: it is the first thing that appears, at the top left.

```html-code
<body>
  <a class="gm-skip-link" href="#content">Skip to content</a>
  <header class="gm-navbar">…</header>
  <main id="content" tabindex="-1">…</main>
</body>
```

## How to add it

- Make it **the first thing** inside `<body>`.
- The `href` points to the `<main>`'s `id`.
- The `<main>` has `tabindex="-1"`, so focus really reaches the content.

## Why

Keyboard users would otherwise have to go through every menu link on every page. With this link they skip them at once (WCAG 2.4.1). When focused it appears as a black button (white at night), clearly visible.

<!-- /docs/helpers/gradient-text -->
# Gradient text

Paints text with the framework's color gradient. At night it switches to a plain color, so it reads well on a dark background.

## Example

```html
<p class="gm-font-bold gm-m-0" style="font-size: 1.4rem">Made with <span class="gm-gradient-text">GlassMarshmallow</span></p>
<h2 class="gm-gradient-title gm-mt-2 gm-mx-0 gm-mb-0">Gradient heading</h2>
```

## Two versions

| Class | For | Gradient |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.gm-gradient-text` | Text of any size | Dark tones, each 7:1 or more (AAA) |
| `.gm-gradient-title` | Large headings (24 px or more) | The bright logo colors, 3:1 or more |

At night, `.gm-gradient-text` is blue and `.gm-gradient-title` uses the text color.

## Accessibility

- A gradient cannot be measured point by point: that is why the text one only uses tones that pass AAA on their own.
- With system high contrast on, the text switches to the system color.
- Do not use it on long paragraphs: it is to highlight a few words or a heading.

<!-- /docs/helpers/text-outline -->
# Text outline

`.gm-text-outline` adds, **in dark mode**, a thin black outline and a soft shadow to text. It keeps text readable over lights, images or the TV effect. In light mode it changes nothing.

## Example

This is how it looks over a background with lights in dark mode:

```html
<div class="gm-grid gm-rounded-sm" data-theme="dark" style="place-items: center; min-height: 10rem; color: #f5f5f7; background: radial-gradient(circle at 30% 40%, #1cabb0, transparent 55%), radial-gradient(circle at 70% 60%, #8c57e9, transparent 55%), #000">
  <p class="gm-text-outline gm-m-0 gm-font-extrabold" style="font-size: 2rem">Readable over the lights</p>
</div>
```

It is the one used by the title and text of this site's home page.

## Accessibility

- The outline helps text reach its contrast even when the background changes from point to point (WCAG 1.4.3).
- Even so, measure the contrast over the real background (with a screenshot), not just the background color.

<!-- /docs/guides/ux -->
# User experience

Rules so that what you build with GlassMarshmallow is easy to understand and use. Some are ours (we decided them while designing the framework) and others come from reference guides (GOV.UK, W3C, Nielsen Norman Group). For forms, see the [form rules](/docs/forms/rules) too.

## Options to choose from

- **2 or 3 short options, in a row**, with the [segmented control](/docs/forms/segmented). **More than 3 or long labels, one below the other** (`--stack`).
- The chosen option shows by more than color: the white pill and the shadow.
- If there is a recommended or most common option, select it from the start.

## Lists

- **With more than 3 items, use a list**, one below the other, not run together in a sentence (“Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator and…”). They are easy to scan and screen readers say how many there are.
- Inside the accordion, with [`.gm-accordion__list`](/docs/components/accordion).

## Mobile navigation

- The [tab bar](/docs/components/tabbar) has **4 buttons at most, counting “More”**. What does not fit goes in the “More” panel.
- Each button with an icon and one word.
- The current page is marked in the bar (`aria-current="page"`).

## Icons

- **Only GlassMarshmallow icons** (`gmi`): no emojis and no icons from other sets mixed in.
- Next to text, **centered with its first line and a bit larger than the letters** (for example, 1.25 rem with 0.92 rem text). Checked by measuring, not by eye.
- An icon on its own (no text) has a name for screen readers (`aria-label` or hidden text). With text, the icon is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`).

## Buttons and actions

- **One main action per area**: the black (white at night) or accent button (pink by day, blue at night). The rest, secondary or text buttons.
- The button text says **what happens when pressed** (“Save changes”, “Watch the next episode”), not “OK”.
- Actions that cannot be undone (delete, pay) ask for confirmation and say what will be lost.
- Everything that can be pressed is at least **44 px** (WCAG 2.5.5).

## Knowing what is happening

- **While loading**, show that work is happening: [progress bar](/docs/components/progress), spinning icon or placeholders with `gm-animate-shimmer`. With text (“Loading the library…”).
- **When done**, confirm what happened with an [alert](/docs/components/alert) (“Changes saved”), announced to screen readers (`role="status"`).
- **With no content**, explain why the screen is empty and what to do (“You have no books yet. Add the first one”).
- **If something fails**, say what happened and how to fix it, without blaming anyone.

## Showing and hiding

- Do not hide in an [accordion](/docs/components/accordion), a [carousel](/docs/components/carousel) or a tab what everyone needs: use them for what only some people want.
- On phones you can rearrange, but not remove: phone users must be able to do the same as on desktop.

## Motion

- [Animations](/docs/utilities/animations) are short and have a reason: something enters, leaves or changes.
- Everything stops if the person asks for **reduced motion** in their system (the framework already does this).
- Nothing moves on its own for more than 5 seconds without a way to stop it, like the autoplaying carousel (which has pause).

## Colors and modes

- **Light and dark with the same care**: everything is checked in both modes.
- **Never color alone** to convey information: add text or an icon (an error in coral also says it is an error).
- Text of **7:1** or more (AAA) whenever possible; the minimum is 4.5:1. Borders and icons that must be seen, 3:1.

## Consistency

- The same thing has the same name and works the same way across the site: if a button is “Save” on one page, it is not “Apply” on another.
- Use the framework components before making a new one; if a new one is needed, it is added to GlassMarshmallow so it is available in every project.

<!-- /docs/guides/logo -->
# How the logo was made

The GlassMarshmallow logo is **two glass marshmallows**: two soft panels with very rounded corners, one in front of the other, on a glass tile. It is made with the framework itself: its colors come from this site's [tools](/tools) and its shape, from the utilities. The SVG the site uses (`logo.svg`) is generated from that same code.

## The logo, made with classes

On the left, the logo made only with GlassMarshmallow classes; on the right, the SVG. They are the same: compared pixel by pixel, the average difference is half a point out of 255.

```html
<div class="gm-d-flex gm-flex-wrap gm-gap-8 gm-items-end">
  <figure class="gm-m-0 gm-d-grid gm-gap-2 gm-justify-items-center">
    <div class="gm-glass-logo gm-w-[12rem]">
      <div class="gm-relative gm-aspect-square gm-[container-type:inline-size] gm-rounded-[22.265625%] gm-bg-[linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.42)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0.16)_100%)] gm-before:[position:absolute] gm-before:inset-[0] gm-before:rounded-[inherit] gm-before:p-[0.976562cqw] gm-before:bg-[linear-gradient(135deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.9)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0.25)_50%,rgba(255,255,255,0.6)_100%)] gm-before:[mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box_exclude,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask-composite:xor]" role="img" aria-label="GlassMarshmallow">
        <span class="gm-absolute gm-start-[23.4375%] gm-top-[23.4375%] gm-w-[37.1094%] gm-h-[37.1094%] gm-rounded-[23.1579%] gm-bg-[linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.55)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0)_50%),linear-gradient(45deg,#3cd2ff_0%,#8c64ff_100%)] gm-before:[position:absolute] gm-before:inset-[-0.488281cqw] gm-before:rounded-[23.8462%] gm-before:p-[0.976562cqw] gm-before:bg-[linear-gradient(135deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.95)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0.25)_100%)] gm-before:[mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box_exclude,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask-composite:xor]"></span>
        <span class="gm-absolute gm-start-[39.4531%] gm-top-[39.4531%] gm-w-[37.1094%] gm-h-[37.1094%] gm-rounded-[23.1579%] gm-bg-[linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.55)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0)_50%),linear-gradient(45deg,rgba(140,100,255,0.85)_0%,rgba(255,150,70,0.85)_100%)] gm-before:[position:absolute] gm-before:inset-[-0.488281cqw] gm-before:rounded-[23.8462%] gm-before:p-[0.976562cqw] gm-before:bg-[linear-gradient(135deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.95)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0.25)_100%)] gm-before:[mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box_exclude,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask-composite:xor]"></span>
      </div>
    </div>
    <figcaption class="gm-small gm-muted">With classes</figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="gm-m-0 gm-d-grid gm-gap-2 gm-justify-items-center">
    <img class="gm-glass-logo gm-w-[12rem]" src="/logo.svg" alt="" width="192" height="192">
    <figcaption class="gm-small gm-muted">SVG</figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>
```

## The colors, with the tools

Each gradient of the logo was made with a tool and copied as is:

| Part | Tool | Settings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tile fill | [Single-color gradient](/tools/single-color-gradient) | White, linear, 180°, opacity from 42% to 16%, extent 100% |
| Shine on each panel | [Single-color gradient](/tools/single-color-gradient) | White, linear, 180°, opacity from 55% to 0%, extent 50% |
| Light edge of each panel | [Single-color gradient](/tools/single-color-gradient) | White, linear, 135°, opacity from 95% to 25%, extent 100% |
| Back panel | [Gradient generator](/tools/gradient-generator) | 45°, `#3cd2ff` at 0% and `#8c64ff` at 100% |
| Front panel | [Gradient generator](/tools/gradient-generator) | 45°, `#8c64ff` and `#ff9646` at 85% opacity |
| Light edge of the tile | [Gradient generator](/tools/gradient-generator) | 135°, white at 90% at 0%, at 25% at 50% and at 60% at 100% |

The three colors (cyan, violet and amber) are the three lights that give GlassMarshmallow its look.

## The shape, with the utilities

1. **The tile:** `gm-aspect-square` (square), `gm-rounded-[22.265625%]` (the curve) and its fill with `gm-bg-[…]`.
2. **Its light edge:** a `gm-before:` layer with the gradient and a mask that only shows the outline (`gm-before:[mask:…]`). That way the edge has its own gradient without covering the glass.
3. **The two panels:** `gm-absolute`, with their place and size in %, their corners (`gm-rounded-[23.1579%]`) and two gradients together in `gm-bg-[…]`: the shine on top and the color below.
4. **The panels' edges:** like the tile's, with `gm-before:` and the mask.
5. **Scaling:** sizes are in % and in `cqw`, hundredths of the logo's width (that is why the tile has `gm-[container-type:inline-size]`). The same code works at 32 px and at 512 px; only the container's width changes (`gm-w-[12rem]`).

The classes in brackets are [arbitrary values](/docs/utilities/arbitrary): `npx glassmarshmallow build` writes them.

## Day and night, the same code

The code is exactly the same in light and dark mode. What changes is set by the framework, through `gm-glass-logo`:

| | Light mode | Dark mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The logo (tile, panels, gradients, shine and edges) | the same | the same |
| What shows through the glass | the light background: the tile looks almost white | the black background: it looks dark gray |
| `gm-glass-logo` | a thin white border and the medium shadow, to set it apart from the background | nothing: the glass already stands out |

## The SVG, from the code

`logo.svg` (the navbar's, the favicon and the share images) is written by the script `site/brand/logo/desde-el-framework.mjs` from the same gradients the tools copy and the same sizes. It is identical to the logo made with classes.

## The full code

```html-code
<div class="gm-glass-logo gm-w-[12rem]">

    <span class="gm-absolute gm-start-[23.4375%] gm-top-[23.4375%] gm-w-[37.1094%] gm-h-[37.1094%] gm-rounded-[23.1579%] gm-bg-[linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.55)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0)_50%),linear-gradient(45deg,#3cd2ff_0%,#8c64ff_100%)] gm-before:[position:absolute] gm-before:inset-[-0.488281cqw] gm-before:rounded-[23.8462%] gm-before:p-[0.976562cqw] gm-before:bg-[linear-gradient(135deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.95)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0.25)_100%)] gm-before:[mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box_exclude,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask-composite:xor]"></span>
    <span class="gm-absolute gm-start-[39.4531%] gm-top-[39.4531%] gm-w-[37.1094%] gm-h-[37.1094%] gm-rounded-[23.1579%] gm-bg-[linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.55)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0)_50%),linear-gradient(45deg,rgba(140,100,255,0.85)_0%,rgba(255,150,70,0.85)_100%)] gm-before:[position:absolute] gm-before:inset-[-0.488281cqw] gm-before:rounded-[23.8462%] gm-before:p-[0.976562cqw] gm-before:bg-[linear-gradient(135deg,rgba(255,255,255,0.95)_0%,rgba(255,255,255,0.25)_100%)] gm-before:[mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box_exclude,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask:linear-gradient(#000_0_0)_content-box,linear-gradient(#000_0_0)] gm-before:[-webkit-mask-composite:xor]"></span>
  </div>
</div>
```
